why it works Each prediction task (clicks, time spent, engagement) reflects different facets of the same user intent. Training one model for all three lets them share learned patterns about what users want, then apply those shared patterns to each prediction. This is cheaper than three separate models and more accurate because the tasks reveal each other's signal.
What's in a Name? Product Normalization for Enterprise RAG at NetAppSIGIR
uses The system rewrites user queries by mapping informal product names to official ones, then restricts retrieval to known documented products, dramatically improving what gets found.
why it works Users call products by many names; the index uses only official names. A hand-crafted normalization layer (users say 'NetApp filer', the system searches 'NetApp ONTAP') closes this vocabulary gap without retraining anything. Restricting to known products eliminates false positives. These lightweight rule-based improvements often beat expensive model retraining on retrieval tasks.
SAER: Scalable Assessment of E-commerce Recommendations using Large Language ModelsSIGIR
uses Uses a language model as a judge to compare recommendation options: first filtering weak candidates, then picking the best by pairwise comparison.
why it works It works because language models understand user preferences expressed in product text and metadata. Pairwise comparison is more stable than absolute scoring—you don't need accurate scores, just which option is better. This avoids position bias and is more robust.
Unifying User Satisfaction and Creator Incentive: A Constrained Optimization Framework for Short-Video RecommendationSIGIR
uses Simultaneously maximize both user satisfaction and creator earnings by setting constraints that keep creator payoff above a threshold while ranking results.
why it works It works because you separate the two competing goals into a primary objective (user satisfaction) and secondary hard constraints (creator earnings). The optimization algorithm decouples the global fairness constraint into independent real-time decisions, ensuring creators get minimum exposure without requiring coordination across all requests.
DIVER: Unlocking Diversity in Ad Headline Generation with Large Language ModelsSIGIR
uses Simultaneously optimize multiple goals—diversity, faithfulness, and click rate—by treating them all as weighted rewards in a single training objective.
why it works It works because optimizing all goals together forces trade-offs to resolve naturally. The model learns which combinations of features satisfy multiple objectives, producing headlines that are diverse yet coherent and clickable, rather than gaming one goal at the expense of others.
Cross-Domain Preference Transfer for Promoting Engagement with Built-in ChatbotsSIGIR
uses Learn the user's preference patterns from content-consumption behavior, then adapt those patterns to predict which topics the user wants to discuss.
why it works It works because preference patterns are universal: if a user likes certain content types, that taste translates across domains. The model learns what makes something appealing to this specific user, then applies that knowledge to rank discussion topics, solving the allocation problem of 'which topic suits this user now'.
Unified Semantic Modeling Framework for Large-Scale Job Understanding at LinkedInSIGIR
uses Teach a model to extract job attributes by training it on many synthetic examples that include step-by-step reasoning, using multiple related tasks simultaneously.
why it works It works because multi-task training forces the model to learn underlying patterns that are useful across many related problems. Adding reasoning traces teaches the model to explain its decisions, which makes the learned function more robust. Learning from many examples, even synthetic ones, generalizes better than memorizing individual cases.
Efficient LLM Adaptation for Opinion Knowledge Graph Construction: Lessons from the Telecom IndustrySIGIR
uses Train a model on many synthetic instruction examples, each with reasoning traces, to extract structured opinions and build knowledge graphs from noisy customer feedback.
why it works It works because instruction tuning teaches the model patterns from diverse examples. Reasoning traces show the model how to decompose messy text into structured output. Multiple similar examples reinforce the same underlying pattern, so the model learns robust behavior rather than brittle rules.
SCOPE: Scalable Cross-Task Orthogonal Progressive Experts for Multi-Task Learning in RecommendationsSIGIR
uses Different tasks are routed to different specialized experts which share learned knowledge but stay orthogonal to reduce redundancy and improve efficiency.
why it works When tasks pull a model in different directions, letting each task have its own expert prevents them from interfering. keeping it simple forces experts to be diverse and complementary, so they can be reused efficiently across tasks. This directly reduces the total model size and computation needed.
Beyond Single Slot: Joint Optimization for Multi-Slot Guaranteed Display AdvertisingSIGIR
uses Ads are matched to available page slots by solving a bipartite graph problem that balances meeting advertiser contracts while respecting page space constraints.
why it works The slot-filling problem is fundamentally a matching problem: assign each ad to a slot such that constraints are satisfied and value is maximized. Casting it as a graph algorithm guarantees finding allocations that scale linearly without missing feasible high-value assignments that greedy approaches would overlook.
OxygenREC: An Instruction-Following Generative Framework for E-commerce RecommendationSIGIR
uses A hybrid system uses a slow language model to reason about user intent, extracting instructions that guide a fast encoder-decoder model to generate recommendations.
why it works Language models reason deeply but are slow and expensive per-query. Encoder-decoders are fast but less deep. The hybrid uses the slow model to extract high-value reasoning signals (instructions) once, then trains the fast model to follow those signals at scale. This splits cost and latency: expensive reasoning offline, cheap inference online.
Item-Targeting with Keyword Enhancement: A Hybrid Approach to Ads TargetingSIGIR
uses Historical successful keyword-to-item pairs are used to suggest related queries for item-targeted ads by finding queries semantically similar to the original target query.
why it works Keyword campaigns reveal which queries truly convert for items. Item targeting uses similarity to reach new queries but misses unexplored ones. Borrowing proven keywords as seeds and then extending via semantic similarity to find nearby unexplored queries combines both precision (proven) and coverage (expanded).
SOMIN: Agentic AI for Automating Professional Visibility and Countering Content HomogenizationSIGIR
uses Retrieve relevant professional examples and combine them to generate unique marketing ideas instead of averaging toward generic output.
why it works It works because retrieving real examples grounds the generation process in specific information rather than statistical averages; combining diverse examples pushes the output away from the statistical mean where most training text clusters.
ATVG: Agentic System for Factually Grounded Travel Advertisement Video GenerationSIGIR
uses Generate video ad clips across themes, verify each stage to find visual errors, then refine inputs based on feedback before assembling the final video.
why it works It works because testing and feedback at intermediate stages catches errors early when they are cheap to fix; cascading verification and refinement guides the system toward quality outputs by iterating toward fewer defects.
XFoodRec: An Explainable Mobile Recommender for Personalized Healthy EatingSIGIR
uses Score and rank recipes by personalized preference and healthiness, then explain each recommendation using natural language to persuade users toward healthier choices.
why it works It works because combining nutritional data with personal taste preference creates two competing signals; explaining the healthy trade-off in natural language makes the reasoning transparent, letting users trust and adopt the recommendation.
A Demonstration of WikiRAG: An Evidence-based Link Prediction for Wikidata with Retrieval Augmented GenerationSIGIR
uses Predict missing relations between entities using numeric fingerprints, retrieve Wikipedia evidence for each candidate, then score which candidates are supported by that evidence.
why it works It works because knowledge graph numeric fingerprints capture plausible relations efficiently but without external grounding; retrieving and scoring against real evidence filters predictions to only those supported by documented facts, removing false positives.
T-RADAR: Simulating Trademark Examination as an Interactive Retrieval Interface for Conflict Risk AssessmentSIGIR
uses Retrieve trademark candidates, simulate adversarial examination across appearance, sound, and meaning features, then aggregate conflict scores to prioritize review.
why it works It works because trademark confusion involves multiple independent criteria—none alone suffices; simulating an adversarial exchange explores all features, and aggregating features-specific scores into conflict risk captures the multi-criteria nature of real legal judgment.
MathMex-PDF: Towards Accessible Visual MathematicsSIGIR
uses Extract mathematical formulas and text from PDFs, then combine formula matching and text similarity in a single ranking to retrieve math-heavy content.
why it works It works because math documents encode meaning in both symbols and words; treating them as separate retrieval channels and combining rankings lets users find content where either the math structure or explanation matches their query.
Speak Beyond English: Multilingual Prompts Improve Query Classification in Small Language ModelsSIGIR
uses Score and fuse query classification outputs from the same model prompted in three languages, weighting by confidence.
why it works A single language may misclassify due to ambiguity; prompting in typologically different languages surfaces different signal strengths. Confidence-weighted fusion combines these signals so strong votes outweigh weak ones.
Towards Structurally Robust Cross-Device Federated RecommendationSIGIR
uses Aggregate federated user updates using similarity of user behavior patterns rather than uniform averaging; weight similar users' updates higher in collaboration.
why it works It works because averaging all users equally in federated settings dilutes signals: users with different preferences corrupt each other's models. Grouping similar users and averaging within groups preserves collaborative patterns while filtering out noise from dissimilar users.
Reasoning for IR &#38; IR for ReasoningSIGIR
uses Moving beyond keyword matching by learning to enforce logical rules, combine multiple pieces of evidence, and perform multi-step reasoning when answering questions.
why it works Reasoning works because it explicitly models the logical structure of the problem—what must follow from what, which paths lead to valid conclusions, and how to combine evidence without mixing causes with accidents. Treating reasoning as a structured process, not just pattern-matching, guarantees you won't draw false conclusions.
Retrieve, Rerank, Answer, Experiment: Hands-On IR Research with PyTerrierSIGIR
uses Retrieving relevant documents from large collections using efficient keyword methods, reranking top results with learned scoring, and generating answer text in one unified pipeline.
why it works A two-stage approach works: keyword search is fast and broad, learned reranking is precise on top results, and neural generation synthesizes the final answer. Each stage compounds effectiveness because each passes only its best results forward.
Multi-Agentic Recommender Systems: Foundations, Perspectives, and Lessons from Large Scale Deployments in eCommerceSIGIR
uses Recommending products by using multiple AI agents that reason about the user's goals, call tools to search and filter inventory, and coordinate to rank products across multiple stages of decision.
why it works One agent can't see everything or reason about all constraints, but multiple agents can divide the problem: one understands the user, one searches inventory, one ranks by price, one by reviews. Combining their signals beats any single score because each agent specializes in one aspect.
SIGIR 2026 Workshop on eCommerce (ECOM26)SIGIR
uses Ranking products for online shoppers by scoring item relevance and purchase intent, blending organic results with sponsored ads, and optimizing for cart additions and sales.
why it works Online shopping differs from web search: the signal is whether people buy, not just click. Scoring for purchase intent works because it directly optimizes for the business goal. Blending organic and sponsored results fairly is a matching problem: pairing the right product to the right user at the right rank.
AgentSearch: Indexing, Retrieval, and Ranking of AI AgentsSIGIR
uses Scoring agents by their relevance across multiple criteria—capabilities, behaviors, constraints—and ranking to surface the best fit for each task.
why it works It works because you only need to order agents correctly by fitness, not predict perfect scores; a rough multi-criterion ranking that gets the best agents on top already solves the discovery problem.
The Second Workshop on Evaluation of Multimodal GenerationSIGIR
uses Defining and measuring correctness when systems generate or retrieve content across text, images, and other modalities simultaneously.
why it works It works because no single metric captures all aspects of goodness; combining multiple evaluation signals—fidelity, alignment, coherence—gives a fuller picture than any one measure alone.
269 papers

Separating cause from coincidence

Data is full of things that merely happen together, but to act well you need what actually causes an outcome — the lever you can pull, not the coincidence you happened to notice.

Why it works — the principle

It works because if you can compare like with like — the same kind of person with and without the one thing you changed — then any leftover difference in outcome must be due to that change, not to who they already were. That careful comparison is exactly what turns a correlation into a cause you can safely act on.

Reconstructing Training Data from Adapter-based Federated Large Language ModelsWWW
uses Reconstructs training text from the slope that flow through compact small add-on modules, exploiting the unique leakage channels they create.
why it works compact small add-on modules concentrate information into fewer features, and focus in fixed layers still reveal which words were present. This makes the hidden data recoverable despite the apparent privacy protections, because information doesn't disappear—it just channels through different paths.
Too Much Sharing, Too Little Security: Authentication Cookie Theft At ScaleWWW
uses Detects when authentication cookies leak to compromised subdomains by simulating attacks and tracking which sensitive credentials flow across domain boundaries.
why it works Cookies work by trusting that parent domain boundaries mean parent domain security. When any subdomain can see parent credentials, one weak link breaks everything. The vulnerability exists because scope rules don't match the actual trust model.
Conflict-Aware RAG: Multi-Stage Learning with Conflict Signals for Robust Retrieval-Augmented GenerationWWW
uses Trains a retrieval system to detect when sources conflict and to prefer answers supported across multiple sources over those relying on only one conflicting source.
why it works When web sources contradict each other, the model can sense that disagreement signals danger. By training on pairs where consistent sources are better than conflicting ones, the system learns that real knowledge should agree with itself—it's the fundamental signature of truth.
An Improved Combinatorial Algorithm for Edge-Colored Clustering in HypergraphsWWW
uses Assign colors to nodes in a hypergraph so node colors match the colors of the edges connected to them.
why it works When a node's color matches its edges, you've found a consistent assignment. The approximation works because each swap toward consistency brings you closer to a globally stable coloring, even if you can't reach perfection in polynomial time.
Causal Pre-training Under the Fairness Lens: An Empirical Study of TabPFNWWW
uses Predict whether someone will buy something fairly, learning from synthetic data created by causal rules, then test on real data with missing values.
why it works Pre-training on data that respects causal rules teaches the model to see real causes, not just coincidental patterns. But causality alone doesn't guarantee fairness across groups; fairness is a separate goal. The model learns robust patterns but still needs extra work to be truly fair.
TraceLLM: Evaluating and Exploring Large Language Models on Trace Analysis in Microservice-based Web ApplicationsWWW
uses adjust a language model to reason over system traces and predict faults by learning causal patterns between events in microservice logs.
why it works Trace analysis is a reasoning task where causality matters more than pattern matching: event A causing B is different from them merely coinciding. adjust language models learn to weigh temporal and dependency signals that distinguish true causation from spurious correlation.
Multi-Modal Enhanced Graph Transfer Learning for Digital Finance Fraud DetectionWWW
uses Align multi-modal fraud patterns (graph, temporal, text) across blockchain networks by learning shared representations that ignore domain-specific distribution shifts.
why it works Fraud schemes repeat across networks with consistent structure but different background noise. By learning to recognize the core fraud pattern and ignore the varying noise, transfer learning finds the signal that's portable: the behavioral signature remains the same even when market conditions shift.
The Verification Crisis: Expert Perceptions of GenAI Disinformation and the Case for Reproducible ProvenanceWWW
uses Establish reproducible benchmarks and data provenance standards that measure how well you can detect and track different types of synthetic media.
why it works Provenance tracking works because information has a history; if you record where text, images, and video come from, you can audit that history to distinguish genuine content from generated. Standardized measurement lets you compare detection methods fairly and know when one approach truly outperforms another.
Decoding Web Memorization: A Semantic Membership Inference Attack on LLMsWWW
uses Generate diverse rewrites of training data samples, extract hidden patterns from the model's focus layers, and train a classifier to distinguish members from non-members using similarity scores.
why it works Semantic similarity works because if you teach the model to produce the same output for different phrasings of the same fact, membership detection that relies on exact surface form fails. By measuring nearness in focus space instead of word matching, you catch memorization even when the model has seen reformulated versions.
Disentangled Graph LLM for Molecule Graph Editing under Distribution ShiftsWWW
uses Disentangle molecule structure into independent factors, ensuring each factor stays consistent even when instructions are rephrased, then assign specialized experts to each factor.
why it works Drug properties depend on true chemical structure, not how you describe the task. By learning factors that remain unchanged across different ways of asking for the same edit, you capture what actually matters in the molecule. Specializing one expert per factor means each one learns a reliable structure-property rule.
PAOSC: Plug-and-play Attention Optimization for Semantic Consistency in LLMsWWW
uses Identify low-value words using a learned scorer, then adjust focus to emphasize words that improve the model's semantic meaning and loss.
why it works Not all words matter equally for the right answer; some are just filler. By distinguishing signal words from noise and reweighting focus, you preserve semantic meaning (which words actually contribute to coherent output) while eliminating wasted computation on low-value words.
RMBRec: Robust Multi-Behavior Recommendation towards Target BehaviorsWWW
uses Maximize the information between auxiliary behaviors and target behavior while minimizing spread of error in predictions across different behavior types.
why it works Auxiliary signals like clicks are noisy because users may click for many reasons unrelated to purchase intent. By maximizing useful information shared between them and purchases, you isolate the true cause of buying. Minimizing spread of error across behavior types ensures that rules learned from one behavior type hold across others.
Bridging Semantic Understanding and Popularity Bias with LLMsWWW
uses Decompose popularity bias into item-side and user-side causes, then score recommendations by how well they disentangle these causes from each other.
why it works It works because when you identify what drives bias separately (whether it's the item's inherent appeal or the user's tendency to like popular things), you can score recommendations that address the real cause rather than treating bias as a single monolithic problem. Separating causes from coincidence lets you fix the root issue, not just the symptom.
Towards Automated Brand-Safety Detection: A Novel Dataset and Comparative Analysis of Language ModelsWWW
uses Train specialized models on labeled stories to recognize whether content fits different safety categories, rather than asking a general model to guess without seeing examples.
why it works It works because showing examples teaches a model the actual patterns that distinguish safe from unsafe content in context. General models must guess; models trained on your specific examples learn the subtle distinctions (tone, subtext, cultural context) that matter for your domain, not generic rules.
(wt) GC-DPG: Graph-Constrained Dual-Phase Generation for Safe and Verifiable Chinese Medical Question AnsweringWWW
uses Plan which medical facts are safe to mention for a disease, then score the model's answer by whether it stays within the plan and doesn't invent facts not in the knowledge base.
why it works It works because hallucination happens when a model generates plausible-sounding text unconstrained by truth. By first enumerating which facts are permissible (grounding in a curated database), then measuring whether the answer stays within that boundary, you separate what is actually known (in the database) from what the model merely imagines to be true.
ZK-V: Zero-Knowledge Verification for Trustworthy Autonomous Driving SimulationWWW
uses Prove cryptographically that a simulation followed safety rules (no crashes, speed limits obeyed) without revealing the actual telemetry numbers, using a blockchain record no one can tamper with.
why it works It works because zero-knowledge proofs mathematically guarantee a statement is true without exposing the evidence. Anyone can verify the proof without seeing the raw data. Blockchain timestamps the proof immutably. This separates 'the simulation obeyed the rule' (the fact you care about) from 'your data is exposed' (the harm you want to prevent).
MultiFPT: Towards Multi-Attribute Fairness in Pre-Trained Graph Neural Networks via Prompt TuningWWW
uses Identify protected characteristics (gender, race, etc.) and adjust the model's internal representations so that those characteristics become statistically independent from predictions, using lightweight small add-on modules instead of retraining.
why it works It works because fairness means the model's decisions don't depend on protected characteristics. Statistical independence (measured by information measures) is the mathematical definition: if you can't predict a characteristic from the representation, the model isn't using it. Enforcing independence via small add-on modules lets you fix bias without expensive retraining.
Social Bias Benchmarks for Large Language ModelsWWW
uses Measure fairness bias in language models across languages and cultures by evaluating their predictions against curated benchmarks.
why it works Comparing model outputs to known bias categories reveals systematic patterns in how models learn from their training data, separating genuine model failures from language-specific challenges.
Collusion-Aware Set-level Learning Framework for Detecting Spamming ActivitiesWWW
uses Learns to score groups of accounts as potential fraud rings by optimizing to detect coordinated manipulation patterns in their collective behavior.
why it works Coordinated fraud creates statistical signatures—temporal alignment, mutual reinforcement—that individual-account scoring misses; group-level scoring exploits those collective patterns.
Unveiling and Mitigating Untargeted Poisoning Attacks on Federated Knowledge Graph EmbeddingWWW
uses Attackers inject false data to corrupt learned entity representations in a system; defense detects outlier density in representation space to identify attackers.
why it works Clean data produces densely clustered representations; poisoned data creates anomalous density gaps; density is a scalar that separates good clients from bad ones.
Cross-Domain Fake News Detection on Unseen Domains via LLM-Based Domain-Aware User ModelingWWW
uses Uses language models to extract high-level meaning from news and user behavior, then learns domain-aware patterns that transfer to unseen news domains.
why it works High-level semantics like story type and user intent are more stable across domains than surface patterns; learning from semantics generalizes when raw words shift.
Counterfactual Augmented Causal Reasoning for Aspect-Based Sentiment AnalysisWWW
uses Generates synthetic examples where correlations flip to teach the model which patterns are causal versus accidental, then filters to causal features only.
why it works Counterfactuals break spurious correlations—if changing a feature breaks the label when true causation says it shouldn't, that feature is spurious; comparison isolates cause.
Beyond Detection: Autonomous Anomaly Remediation for MCP Against Tool Poisoning AttacksWWW
uses Detect anomalies in tool behaviors by finding which operations are most likely root causes of failure, then mask those causes and re-run to verify the fix.
why it works It works because anomalies leave traces in what the system pays focus to—if you mask the actual problem cause, the system will re-infer without that corruption, proving you found the real culprit. A USIM-less Identity Authentication System based on Zero-Knowledge ProofsWWW

why it works It works because a zero-knowledge proof lets you convince others a fact is true without showing the evidence. No personal data is revealed, so attackers cannot steal or breach your identity.
WAMO: Toward Secure Browser Inference via Web Model Obfuscation in WebAssemblyWWW
uses Convert systems that learn from examples models to hardened binary code that is difficult to reverse-engineer, making model weights and computation graphs hard to extract.
why it works It works because obscuring code raises the cost of attack. High cyclomatic complexity makes control flow hard to follow; high Halstead effort means reverse-engineering requires much more work.

uses Score the expected profit a validator coalition gains from hiding blocks versus adopting the standard honest strategy.
why it works Miners only care about which choice earns more; by calculating exact expected payoffs, you can find which strategy dominates. If profit exceeds the honest payout, that strategy is adopted.
ReGA: Zero-Overhead Graph Alignment for Structural Hallucination Detection Without GenerationWWW
uses Score how well the model's extracted graph structure matches the correct relationship directions between entities.
why it works Hallucinations show up as wrong edge directions; by treating the correct graph and extracted graph as two configurations and measuring their alignment distance, you separate correct from corrupted structures.

uses Federated clients cluster their graphs locally while decoupling public shared structure from private local patterns to align clusters despite mismatched cluster counts.

Bento: Fine-Grained Memory Isolation for COTS WebAssembly BinariesWWW
uses Analyzes pointer patterns to partition memory into isolated regions, then rewrites the binary to map each region to separate memory instances without adding runtime checks.

Pattern-aware Illicit Account Detection based on User Behavior SequencesWWW

uses Detects which image attributes are truly tied to class labels versus accidentally co-occurring, then estimates what unbiased data would look like by generating missing samples.
why it works It works because true causal links between attribute and class are stable across edits, but accidental correlations break when you change an image. MuVaC: A Variational Causal Framework for Multimodal Sarcasm Understanding in DialoguesWWW
uses Models sarcasm detection and explanation as causally linked: the explanation process causes the detection outcome, jointly optimized with causal pathways guiding both tasks.
why it works It works because sarcasm isn't just a label but emerges from reasoning—the explanation causally generates the detection. Robust Graph Learning on the Web: Challenges, Methods, and ApplicationsWWW

why it works It works because web data constantly shifts in adversarial and non-adversarial ways. By identifying what the model's decisions truly depend on versus spurious patterns, you can retrain only on the causal factors, making models robust when real conditions differ from training.
Trustless Feedback: Preserving Privacy and Integrity in Crowdsourced RLHF via Zero-Knowledge ProofsWWW

why it works It works because a proof that something satisfies a constraint doesn't need to expose what it is. By encoding rules as mathematical equations and proving satisfaction, you check causation—did this data actually violate safety?—purely from the proof structure, leaving raw data private.
When to Trust: A Causality-Aware Calibration Framework for Accurate Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented GenerationWWW

why it works It works because overconfidence hides when models rely on luck rather than reasoning. Understanding Post-Exploit Laundering Behavior on EthereumWWW

why it works Launderers must move money through many small steps to hide its origin; this creates a behavioral signature different from normal trading. Greedy Attack: Breaking Finality against VeChain Proof-of-Authority Consensus ProtocolWWW

why it works If an attacker poisons a few documents, those come up consistently in poisoned queries but honest facts appear across many varied retrievals; redundancy acts as a fingerprint of truth, so averaging across diverse retrievals strips out the poisoned signal.
Incorporating Graph-Constrained RAG Pipeline for Medicine dataWWW
uses Use a knowledge graph as the backbone and interface so language models retrieve facts by following relation chains, constraining answers to only facts that are explicitly connected.
why it works Language models hallucinate when they guess; by forcing retrieval to walk explicit graph edges, every answer must trace a real path through known facts, making false answers impossible because there is no path to them.
ARuleCon: Agentic Security Rule ConversionWWW

why it works Each vendor's language is a different way to express the same detection logic; by distilling to a vendor-neutral intermediate form, you capture the intent, and by validating both versions yield the same results on test cases, you guarantee the conversion preserved the original meaning.
NeocorRAG: Less Irrelevant Information, More Explicit Evidence, and More Effective Recall via Evidence ChainsWWW
uses Improve retrieval-augmented answers by finding chains of evidence where each document points to the next, then ranking chains by how well they support the final answer.
why it works Single facts can be wrong or irrelevant, but chains where each document cites or builds on the previous one form a traceable argument; ranking chains by their contribution to reasoning quality ensures you retrieve facts that actually matter, not just statistically close matches.
Rethinking the Hidden Risk of Reranking: Achieving Risk-aware Reranking with Information Gain for RAG with LLMsWWW
uses Reranks retrieved documents for language models by balancing the benefit of promoting correct documents against the risk of amplifying misleading ones.
why it works It works because reranking shifts document type distributions in ways that can hurt even when accuracy metrics improve; tracking the full distribution (not just what's on top) reveals when the fix creates a new problem, letting you choose reranking strategies that minimize harm.
From Sold-Out to Sales Uplift: Causal Inference for Intelligent Inventory Management on Online Travel PlatformsWWW
uses Measures what would really happen to total platform sales if you add one inventory item, accounting for whether hotels accept it and whether it just shifts sales between competitors.
why it works Simply correlating inventory changes with sales hides shifts and rejections. Separating real causes from confounding factors reveals the true effect of each inventory action, so resources go to changes that actually grow platform revenue instead of just redistributing existing sales.
CASE: Conflict-assessed Knowledge-sensitive Neuron Tuning for Lifelong Model EditingWWW
uses Updates specific parts of a language model to fix wrong facts while measuring conflicts between different fix attempts to avoid erasing previously learned knowledge.
why it works Multiple edits can contradict each other or erase starting guess corrections. By quantifying which edits conflict with which, you can allocate which parts of the model each edit should touch, avoiding crashes where one fix undoes another.
Unsupervised Multi-Source Causal Feature SelectionWWW
uses Selects which features matter most across multiple data sources by removing confounding factors and weighting each source to reveal shared true causes beneath source-specific noise.
why it works Data sources disagree due to both noise and real confounding. By upweighting sources that agree and downweighting those affected by confounds, you surface the truly causal features that matter everywhere, not spurious correlations that vary by source.
The More You Say, the More You Risk: Ethical Concerns in Large Language Model Reasoning FrameworksWWW
uses Shows that prompting techniques that help language models reason better also sometimes make them unfairer and more prone to stereotypes than simpler approaches.
why it works Reasoning frameworks like chain-of-thought let models articulate more, which can amplify biases present in training. More expression gives more room for stereotypes to appear unless safety measures also scale with reasoning capability.
CLGNN: A Contrastive Learning-based GNN for Temporal Betweenness Prediction under Extreme Value ImbalanceWWW
uses Predicts how central each node is in temporal networks by learning graph structure with contrastive learning to separate nodes of different importance levels.
why it works Importance in temporal networks is rare: most nodes are unimportant, which drowns out the signal about truly central nodes. By actively pushing nodes of different importance into different regions of the learned space, the model stops wasting capacity on the obvious negatives and focuses on what makes central nodes actually special.
CausalSKyHop: Knowledge-Aware Causal Explanation of Dynamic GNNs via Higher-Order Semantic ReasoningWWW
uses Explains predictions from graph models by finding causal multi-node patterns and contrasting meaningful cause-effect pathways against spurious coincidences.
why it works Real causes produce consistent relationships that hold across different contexts; spurious coincidences appear only in specific, accidental situations. By looking for patterns that remain stable as the graph changes while discarding patterns that vanish, the method distinguishes true causation from noise.
Deterring A Small Collusion is All You NeedWWW
uses Studies auction design for blockchains to determine what level of collusion resistance is actually achievable and necessary.
why it works In auction design, robustness is about eliminating opportunities, not absolute prevention. The proof shows that if a mechanism is vulnerable to any collusion size, there exists a small collusion that exploits it: focusing defense on preventing small coordinated attack is sufficient because larger collu, by economic logic, would encounter diminishing returns to coordination.
Fine-Grained Visual Understanding for Multimodal and Trustworthy AIWWW
uses Survey of methods to visually distinguish between objects that look nearly identical but have different labels, and how language and multimodal data improve this task.
why it works Fine-grained visual distinction is hard because small appearance differences matter, but many irrelevant changes also shift pixels. Adding language context works because it grounds what differences actually matter: a model learns which pixel changes reflect real semantic difference (a species name) versus accidental variation (lighting, angle). Multimodal fusion exploits complementary signals: vision captures fine detail, language clarifies what counts.
SLS: A Scalable Logic Subgraph Framework for Temporal Web Analytics and Hybrid SearchWWW
uses Split data by time and attributes, then build a graph index on each chunk so you can search for items that match both feature similarity and time constraints without redundant scanning.
why it works This works because time and features are separable concerns: if you enforce consistency within each partition, exact filtering no longer destroys precision. The graph index then lets you skip irrelevant chunks entirely, cutting search cost from scanning everything.
Breaking Semantic-Aware Watermarks via LLM-Guided Coherence-Preserving Semantic InjectionWWW
uses Perturb image semantics in a way that looks consistent to humans and models but changes watermark signals, forcing the watermark check to fail while keeping the image coherent.
why it works This works because semantic watermarks bind the mark to global image meaning—but global meaning and local watermark signals live in different feature subspaces. Change the right subspace coherently and you break the binding without wrecking the image.
Robust Fake News Detection using Large Language Models under Adversarial Sentiment AttacksWWW
uses Learning to distinguish real news from fake by teaching a system which patterns of tone and emotion always appear in real articles, even when an attacker changes those emotions.
why it works It works because truly false content has patterns deeper than just tone—if a detector learns only from tone it fails against tone-switching attacks. By identifying the irreducible core patterns of falsehood independent of emotional spin, the system gets genuinely robust.
AiOfAi: 4th Workshop on Adverse Impacts and Collateral Effects of Artificial Intelligence TechnologiesWWW
uses Building tools to detect when AI is being used to spread lies or attack systems, and building other AI tools to defend against those attacks.
why it works It works because understanding the two-sided nature—that the same techniques enable both harm and defense—lets you build both detection and resilience. You cannot defend against threats you don't comprehend, and cannot deploy defense if you only see malice.
Invariant Learning on Heterogeneous Graphs via Subgraph Environment InferenceWWW
uses Finding which node features are stable across changes in real-world networks (distribution-shift invariant) by learning what spurious patterns are misleading and ignoring them.
why it works It works because a pattern that depends on the current data collection setup (spurious) fails when the setup changes. By finding only patterns stable across inferred sub-environments, you keep what's truly causal and discard environment-specific noise.
DriftNavi: Talk through Your Data Drift with LLMsWWW
uses Letting a user ask conversational questions about why a machine-learning model's predictions changed when the data shifted, getting explanations at their understanding level.
why it works It works because drift is itself a causal shift—by letting the model reason through detect/explain/adapt stages interactively, users see which input factors actually caused the performance drop, not just that something broke.
CIFAD: Causal-Invariant Subspace Learning for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection on Dynamic Relational GraphsWWW
uses Disentangle stable causal user-behavior patterns from temporary noise, learn from a tiny labeled set by choosing which new examples to label based on their influence, compress user histories into low-dimensional stable components.
why it works It works because real anomalies follow a causal rule even when environments shift; if you strip away the noise, that rule stays the same across time. Using influence to choose which few new labels matter most maximizes learning from scarcity, and low-dimensional components ignore distracting fluctuations.
Large Language Model for OWL ProofsWWW
uses Extract the logical chain proving an answer from a formal ontology, simplify noisy intermediate steps, and explain the result in clear language that shows why the proof is sound.
why it works It works because a valid proof is itself a kind of similarity—it shows how conclusion and premise sit close together in logical space. Extracting the chain, cleaning it, and explaining it in language lets large models use their strength at reasoning while producing human-readable evidence, not just a final answer.
SPCA: Stream Parser Confusion Attack for Web Application Firewall Evasion in HTTP/2WWW
uses The attack identifies confusions between security checks and backend servers by manipulating message priorities in ways that rearrange how payloads travel but leave content unchanged.
why it works Security checks and backend servers parse the same protocol, but if they disagree on which messages matter most, malicious content can slip past the check while the backend still processes it. The reordering is invisible to the check but visible to different parsing choices.
A2GBD: Attack-Agnostic Graph Backdoor DefenseWWW
uses Identify which nodes look suspicious, then adaptively choose defense actions that reduce the likelihood of attack success.
why it works It works because backdoored nodes show patterns different from clean ones when examined closely. Once you identify suspicious nodes, applying targeted defenses there removes the attack's influence without requiring knowledge of how the attack was constructed.
TGweaver: Synthesizing Transaction Graphs for De-anonymization AnalysisWWW
uses Generate realistic transaction data with behavioral patterns, then train supervised models to predict which addresses belong together in mixing services.
why it works It works because supervised learning from labeled transactions can discover patterns in fund movement that heuristic rules miss. Rules are brittle; learned patterns adapt to complex mixing strategies because they extract the true signal of behavior correlation from data.
Exploring and Exploiting Security Vulnerabilities in Self-Hosted LLM ServicesWWW
uses Map a target's endpoints and attack surface, then systematically probe and exploit security weaknesses without authentication or access.
why it works It works because most deployed systems have configuration choices that trade security for convenience. By modeling the attack graph and testing common misconfigurations, you can find the weak points that were left open, revealing real-world vulnerabilities.
Sparse Causal Latent Features for Robust Multimodal Learning under Distribution ShiftsWWW
uses Select a small set of stable causal features and filter out spurious correlations that don't generalize to new data.
why it works Most features are noise that happened to correlate in training; a gating mechanism identifies which few features stay predictive across different environments. Discarding the rest removes brittle shortcuts and exposes the real causal signal.
PrivSplit: A Lossless Method for Prompt Privacy in Distributed Parameter-Efficient Fine-TuningWWW
uses Split numeric fingerprints into public and private parts, then compensate for the private part so the model trains identically.
why it works An attacker seeing only public numeric fingerprints cannot invert to the raw input if the private part holds the invertible information. Perfect compensation ensures no utility loss, so privacy is free—you gain security with no accuracy cost.
Decentralised Trust Layers for the Web: Towards Transparent AI-Powered PlatformsWWW
uses Anchor model versions and input data to an immutable append-only log, then issue cryptographic proofs that let anyone verify what a model did.
why it works Immutable logs create a permanent ground truth that no party can alter retroactively. Cryptographic proofs let anyone verify claims about what actually happened, independently of who is making the claim. This separates genuine behavior from denial or revisionism.
Starlink in the Wild: Multi-Perspective Measurements via DNSWWW
uses Infer Starlink's network architecture and security from DNS records, passive traffic patterns, and active scanning of exposed services.
why it works DNS records and traffic patterns leak details about the network's structure. By correlating these observations, you can separate real infrastructure signals from noise and rebuild a picture of internal organization that the provider tries to hide.
KEPo: Knowledge Evolution Poison on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented GenerationWWW
uses Inject poisoned knowledge into the graph by forging fake evolution paths from true facts, misleading the model into treating fabricated nodes as authoritative.
why it works Language models reason about graph structure as if edges represent real causality and evolution. By planting fake but coherent paths, attackers exploit the model's trust that structured knowledge is vetted. The model sees logical links and treats them as established truth.
Beyond Single Pass, Looping Through Time: KG-IRAG with Iterative Knowledge RetrievalWWW
uses Iteratively refine candidate answers by fetching facts tied to specific time periods, checking if each fact's timing aligns with others, then moving on to the next fact.
why it works Time-tagged facts form a causal chain; by verifying that events happen in the right sequence and within valid time windows, you eliminate answers that fit some facts but contradict their timing. Ordering and interval-checking are a cheap way to filter impossibilities without trying all combinations.
Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the WebWWW
uses Detect when search results are filled with low-quality AI-generated text by measuring how much results cluster into a narrow band of similar writing, and filter when diversity drops.
why it works Original diverse content comes from many independent sources with different voices; heavy AI generation produces statistically similar text across many results. Measuring the collapse of diversity—how tightly results cluster together—catches when the pipeline has been hijacked, because the lack of variation is itself the signal of synthesis.
The Power of Penalties: Negativity-Aware Incentives for High-Quality Crowdsourced Data LabelingWWW
uses Assign each worker a contribution score that can be positive (good labels) or negative (fraud); pay workers fairly based on both their ability and their real-time task results, and penalize harmful work.
why it works Standard payment ignores fraud because negatives are hard to model; signed contribution scores (Shapley values extended to allow negative valuations) let you measure and reward both excellence and punish toxicity with one framework. Pre-commitment stakes raise the cost of fraud without killing participation—workers self-regulate when they have skin in the game.
Feasibility of Cryptography In a Blockchain-Enhanced ICS SecurityWWW
uses Route cryptographic verification of sensor readings through fast lightweight algorithms instead of blockchain-heavy methods, reserving blockchain for non-critical layers where latency is tolerable.
why it works Industrial systems require near-zero latency (tens of milliseconds); blockchain consensus and heavyweight cryptography add 50-400 ms. Lattice-based authentication (LWE) performs the same verification in microseconds. By matching the right tool to each network tier's constraints, you avoid the architectural mismatch that kills safety-critical systems.
FedDis: A Causal Disentanglement Framework for Federated Traffic PredictionWWW
uses Splits traffic patterns into two independent parts: what is unique to each city (local dynamics) and what all cities share (global trends), then predicts by combining them.
why it works It works because mixing local and shared patterns makes the model learn the wrong thing—noise in one city corrupts the global signal. By forcing the two branches to carry different information (measured by information theory), each branch specializes in what it alone can explain, and combining them captures the full truth.
Graph Adversarial Defense via Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion against Influence Maximization AttacksWWW
uses Filters out perturbations by keeping only the features that predict the label, using a independence measure to detect when noise creeps into the model's inputs.
why it works It works because adversarial noise is correlation without causation—it changes the input in ways that don't affect the true label, only the model's decision. By measuring dependence, you identify features the model actually needs and discard noise that only tricks it.
WED-Net: A Weather-Effect Disentanglement Network with Causal Augmentation for Urban Flow PredictionWWW
uses Splits traffic into two independent channels: weather-driven changes (rain affects speed) versus underlying patterns (time of day always causes congestion), then augments training data by changing only non-causal parts.
why it works It works because extreme rain is rare in data, so the model overfits to the few rainy examples it sees. By augmenting data with synthetic rare-weather scenarios where you preserve true causal structure (rain still blocks roads) and vary only noise, you teach the model to generalize to unseen extremes.
They Said Memes Were Harmless --- We Found the Ones That Hurt: Decoding Jokes, Symbols, and Cultural ReferencesWWW
uses Enriches meme understanding with external knowledge (cultural references, symbols) and tunes two independent decision branches to sharpen the line between satire and actual abuse, then explains each classification.
why it works It works because abuse hides behind symbols and satire that generic models don't recognize. Adding external knowledge exposes hidden meaning, while parameter-efficient tuning specializes each branch to hard cases. Dual channels force the model to commit to a decision, which eliminates ambiguous gray zones where satire and harm blur together.
Difference-based Sample Selection for Federated Graph RationalizationWWW
uses Selects training examples where different models disagree most, focusing on cases that expose shortcut patterns instead of real causes.
why it works It works because disagreement signals confusion: when local and global models differ most, the model is likely leaning on client-specific spurious patterns. Training on these examples teaches the model to ignore the misleading signals.
SeaRAG: Reducing Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Statement-Entity Adaptive RankingWWW
uses Detects when the model is guessing by measuring uncertainty (how much surprise) about entities and statements, then fetches clarifying facts in real-time.
why it works It works because high how much surprise signals doubt: when a model is unsure about a fact, it's likely to hallucinate. Measuring uncertainty tells you exactly when to fetch real information. This beats always fetching (wasteful) and never fetching (risky).
Unequal Vulnerability: The Differential Impact of Label Flipping Attacks Across ClassesWWW
uses Measure how easily a model confuses one class with another, then shield the most vulnerable class pairs by pushing them farther apart in the model's learned feature space.
why it works This works because classes that the model already finds hard to distinguish are easiest targets for label flipping—their representations overlap, so swapping labels causes minimal learned change. By actively separating these confusable pairs, the model learns features where the classes occupy regions so different that label-flipped training examples fight less against the correct pattern, making the model more resistant.
The Promise vs. Reality of NFT Decentralization: An Empirical Study of Storage Strategies and DefectsWWW
uses Catalog how NFTs store their data (on-chain vs off-chain), classify storage vulnerabilities into access failure, tampering, and forgery defects, and measure severity using a standard vulnerability scoring system.
why it works This works because promised decentralization (immutable on-chain storage) conflicts with reality (centralized off-chain data)—the promise only holds if both the contract and the content are kept. By separating defect types (can the data disappear vs can it be corrupted vs can fakes replace it) and scoring systematically, the analysis reveals which assets are actually centralized and exposed to which real risks. Cataloging defects gives developers concrete targets to fix, not vague warnings.
When Reasoning Leaks Membership: Membership Inference Attack on Black-box Large Reasoning ModelsWWW
uses Finds a direction in semantic space where familiar training examples lie on one end and unfamiliar ones on the other, then scores a sample's membership by where it falls along that axis.
why it works It works because models that trained on data produce reasoning traces with consistent patterns and confidences on that data, while new data triggers different patterns. By mapping those traces into a space and measuring distance along a learned axis, membership becomes detectable even without seeing the model's internal scores.
Eroding the Truth-Default: A Causal Analysis of Human Susceptibility to Foundation Model Hallucinations and Disinformation in the WildWWW
uses Uses causal reasoning to identify what factors actually drive humans' ability to spot fake text from language models, testing whether exposure or personality explains detection skill.
why it works It works because just counting who spots fakes tells you nothing about why—correlation doesn't show if exposure trains you, or if certain personalities are naturally skeptical. Causal models let you block false paths and see the true mechanism. Exposure acts as adversarial training: seeing bad fakes immunizes you.
WPIS: From In-the-Wild Web Images to Physics-Aware 3D Scene Graphs for Physical ReasoningWWW
uses Extract functional scene knowledge from lab photos by identifying which object and hand interactions are physically possible, then connecting them with natural-language descriptions of what each part does.
why it works It works because physics causality is real: if a hand reaches toward a container and liquid flows, it's not coincidence—there's a causal mechanism. Grounding descriptions in physical possibility (can hands actually reach? can liquid actually flow?) separates real affordances from visual noise or mistaken patterns.
Fact-Checking Strategies in Web: Lateral Navigation in the Browser Boosts Health Misinformation Detection Even Under Confirmation BiasWWW
uses Detect health misinformation by measuring whether users check multiple sources (lateral reading) versus spending time on one source; lateral reading measurably improves accuracy independent of user bias.
why it works It works because information from independent sources reduces noise: if multiple sources agree, it's unlikely to be pure noise or coincidence. Laterally gathered information reveals discrepancies that trigger skepticism, creating a causal pathway from diverse reading to better decisions—even when users start biased.
Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAGWWW
uses Measure how much a malicious instruction changes which documents retrieval returns.
why it works Detection works because poisoned content that influences retrieval jumps higher in the ranked list; the rank shift is the fingerprint of attack.
Anomaly Detection of Interaction Behaviors in Streaming GraphsWWW
uses Measure how much each new edge deviates from the baseline propensity of two entities to interact.
why it works Works because every pair of entities has a natural interaction frequency; a large deviation from that frequency is the anomaly signal.
The Devil Within, The Cure Without: Securing Locally Private Graph Learning under PoisoningWWW
uses Screen out poisoned nodes from a private graph while maintaining differential privacy and recovering utility through trimming and fake-node pruning.
why it works Works because trimmed screening removes extreme anomalies without needing to know if they are attacks; the survivors form a robust graph and filtering adapts to privacy constraints.
Maximum Edge-based Quasi-Clique: Novel Iterative FrameworksWWW
uses Find the largest subset of a network where edges are tightly connected above a threshold, by reformulating it as a sequence of simpler subproblems that allow aggressive pruning.
why it works It works because breaking a hard problem into hereditary subproblems lets you eliminate branches early—if a subproblem has no solution, all larger problems containing it fail too, cutting the search space exponentially.
Mitigating Cognitive Vulnerabilities in Code Generation via Multi-Agent Adversarial DebateWWW
uses Generate code through structured debate between three agents with opposing views, then stress-test the plan with intentional perturbations to catch logical flaws.
why it works It works because adversarial scrutiny from multiple angles exposes weak reasoning that one agent alone would miss; stress-testing with opposite scenarios ensures the plan survives edge cases, not just the common path.
Suppression or Deletion: A Restoration-Based Representation-Level Analysis of Machine UnlearningWWW
uses Use sparse autoencoders to find the specific features responsible for learned information, then steer those features at inference time to test whether information is truly deleted or merely hidden.
why it works It works because information can hide at different representation levels—even if a model's output looks 'forgotten', the underlying features might remain; steering those features directly reveals what was actually erased versus suppressed.
We Need a More Robust Classifier: Dual Causal Learning Empowers Domain-Incremental Time Series ClassificationWWW
uses Learns which features actually cause correct predictions versus which are misleading noise, then trains to predict using only the true causal features.
why it works Confounding features mislead classifiers by happening to co-occur with the right answer in one domain but not another. By explicitly separating causal from spurious features and forcing the model to ignore spurious ones, predictions stay true when the domain shifts.
From Random Forget-Sets to Realistic Natural-Language Deletion RequestsWWW
uses Maps natural-language deletion requests to concrete graph targets using a hybrid ranking score (BM25 and nearness), then selects a small representative subset of requests for reproducible evaluation.
why it works Text-based requests are ambiguous; hybrid scoring combines lexical match (BM25) and semantic nearness (numeric fingerprints) so most requests map correctly. Sampling by a deterministic score ensures the evaluation subset is actionable and reproducible across different unlearning methods.
Eclipse Attacks on Ethereum's Peer-to-Peer NetworkWWW
uses Scores and prioritizes stages of a coordinated network attack, poisoning discovery tables, infiltrating DNS rankings, and hijacking idle slots to isolate blockchain nodes completely.
why it works Isolation requires blocking all paths to honest peers. By scoring stages by achievability (DNS needs only 28 IPs, slots hijacking raises success 45% to 95%), the attack prioritizes the most leverage; multi-stage coordination ensures each step feeds the next for complete isolation.
ARC: A Tool to Rate AI Models for Robustness Through a Causal Lens for Enabling Trustworthy Model SelectionWWW
uses Measures how much predictions change when you perturb inputs or protected attributes, using causal reasoning to distinguish real robustness from coincidence.
why it works It works because robustness means predictions should only depend on what causes them, not accidental correlations. Measuring change under perturbation reveals what predictions truly depend on.
LHG: LLM-enhanced and Heterogeneous Graph-induced for Unsupervised Social Event DetectionWWW
uses Generate pseudo-labels for social messages via language model; filter out hallucinated labels by selecting only those whose semantic similarity is high along meaningful graph-based relationship paths.
why it works Language models produce labels containing real signal mixed with hallucination. Graph meta-paths encode 'who talks to whom about topics'; if an event label has high similarity along these paths, it reflects true collaboration, not just superficial word overlap. Real social signals are more cohesive than hallucinations.
Fair Geolocation Extraction from Humanitarian Documents Using Large Language ModelsWWW
uses Extracts location names from humanitarian documents using few-shot learning to recognize mentions, then resolves ambiguous place names by considering context clues.
why it works It works because context eliminates ambiguity—knowing 'Jerusalem' appears near 'West Bank' rather than 'Kentucky' reveals which city is meant; reasoning about nearby words in text separates real geographic references from coincidental name matches.
Broken Promise: Differential Analysis of Functional Discrepancies Between WebAssembly and Native BinariesWWW
uses Finds discrepancies between WebAssembly and native code by testing both with the same inputs and measuring which ones cause different outputs, then traces root causes.
why it works It works because identical input sets applied to both versions reveal the boundaries of their differences; inputs that split behavior pinpoint exactly which edge cases expose the bug, eliminating false leads and showing the true source of failure.
Can Large Language Models Govern Themselves? A Technical, Ethical, and Governance PerspectiveWWW
uses Examines whether language models can regulate their own behavior through internal feedback loops and embedded constraints, then distinguishes technical self-management from true moral self-governance.
why it works It works because true governance requires both monitoring (does the system detect errors?) and moral grounding (does it know what right looks like?); the paper separates the solvable technical parts (feedback) from the unsolvable philosophical ones (moral agency) based on what mechanisms can actually accomplish each goal.
Open or Blocked Skies? Community Moderation Practices in BlueskyWWW
uses Measures community moderation impact by analyzing public blocking actions across millions of users, then correlates blocking patterns with account properties to distinguish signal from noise.
why it works It works because blocklists target specific account behaviors systematically; comparing blocked versus unblocked accounts reveals which signals (toxicity, activity, ideology) actually drive moderation decisions versus which correlations are coincidence, showing that blocking is precise but its effects are limited.
A Graph Foundation Model for Unified Anomaly DetectionWWW
uses Detects unusual nodes and subgraphs by learning which features reliably predict normal behavior, then flags things where features behave differently than expected.
why it works Normal patterns recur reliably; anomalies deviate. When you learn what features make something normal, you can test new examples against that knowledge. Things that don't match the normal pattern are rare, so you can also artificially create fake anomalies to teach the system what unusual looks like.
PAC to the Future: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of PAC Private SystemsWWW
uses Uses privacy math to prove noise was applied correctly, verified through cryptographic proofs without revealing internals.
why it works Privacy works when each person's data has minimal impact on any answer; proving this via cryptographic proof makes it verifiable without exposing the system. The math guarantees no individual is harmed by joining.
Modeling Endogenous Logic: Causal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Model for Explainable Multi-Behavior RecommendationWWW
uses Identifies which user behaviors truly cause others (view leads to buy) versus which happen together by chance, then weights each chain by causal strength.
why it works Confounders like sales make unrelated things appear linked; causal inference filters these out by asking 'what would happen if we broke this link?' revealing true cause-effect. Real causes explain behavior chains better than coincidence.
The Asymmetric Vulnerability: Bypassing LLM Defenses via Guardrail-Model MismatchWWW
uses Exploits a mismatch: guardrails split text one way but the model reconstructs intent from noise differently, so perturbed text bypasses filters but reaches the model.
why it works Models trained on diverse, noisy text learn resilient patterns that recover meaning from fragments. Guardrails use brittle exact-matching on characters. The model's learned robustness defeats the filter's precision.
Uncertainty-Aware Web-Conditioned Scientific Fact-CheckingWWW
uses Breaks claims into atomic facts, estimates confidence in each fact via numeric fingerprints similarity, and triggers web search only when internal evidence is uncertain.
why it works High-confidence facts from strong evidence need no external check; low-confidence facts need corroboration. Selective external search saves cost while catching hallucinations; confidence acts as a filter for which facts need verification.
Concept Relationship Embedding-Based Interactive Web Application for Explainable Medical DiagnosisWWW
uses Diagnose disease by extracting fine-grained medical concepts from images, building a relationship graph of concepts, and inferring which causal paths lead to disease.
why it works It works because disease diagnosis is fundamentally causal reasoning: symptoms cause observations, disease causes symptoms. By explicitly modeling concept relationships and tracing causal chains—not just tallying concept presence—the model mirrors clinical reasoning and explains its conclusions.
How to Measure Node Importance in the Agentic WebWWW
uses Identify influential agents in networks of autonomous systems by measuring how effectively information spreads through each agent while degrading over distance.
why it works It works because agent networks differ from human social networks: agents care about information utility, not just passing it along. By modeling information decay along paths and valuing throughput and semantic preservation—not just connection count—you rank nodes by actual utility in the new paradigm.
Thinking Bidirectionally: A Reasoning and Self-Correction Approach for Text-Based Event Prediction with Large Language ModelsWWW
uses The system predicts future events by analyzing temporal trends and finding hidden connections within time windows, then corrects errors.
why it works Real events follow causal chains through time and hidden correlations; checking predictions against logic catches hallucinations.
DualDis: A Dual Disentanglement Network for Vehicle Re-identificationWWW
uses Separate vehicle identity features from appearance variations by focusing focus on the most distinctive parts while filtering irrelevant details.
why it works Matching the same vehicle across cameras works because identity is stable even when appearance changes. focus learns which features stay consistent across viewpoint and occlusion. By isolating the distinctive parts from redundant ones, a model can match the same car even when it looks different, treating identity as what genuinely varies least.
The Agentic Insider: Redefining Insider Threats Beyond Human Actors in Autonomous AI SystemsWWW
uses Redefine insider threats to include AI agents by monitoring for role drift, emergent misuse, and emergent behaviors not predicted by original intent.
why it works Detecting insider misuse works because legitimate and malicious behavior differ in patterns. With human actors, intent and trust frame analysis. With autonomous agents, behavior patterns alone must signal threat, because agents lack human intent. The true insider signal is detecting when an agent acts outside its authorized scope, regardless of 'why.'
Belief-Driven Multi-Agent Collaboration via Approximate Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium for Social SimulationWWW
uses Agents maintain probabilistic beliefs about each other's skills and iteratively update these beliefs using game theory, choosing whether to cooperate or debate based on which strategy is most rational given the current belief state.
why it works It works because under incomplete information, sequentially rational decisions require agents to track what they know and don't know about each other. By modeling uncertainty as beliefs and using game equilibrium—where no agent can improve by unilaterally changing strategy—you ensure coordination that converges rather than deadlocks.
SQL-Checker: Error Detection and Labeling for Text-to-SQL with Interpretability AnalysisWWW
uses Identify and categorize SQL errors by learning from synthetic data where errors are introduced systematically, then refine labels by comparing error patterns.
why it works It works because real SQL errors are rare and hard to label by hand. Synthesizing them lets you build training examples with known error types; then comparing mistake patterns across similar queries helps you trust which error labels are real versus which are mislabeled.
DRGW: Learning Disentangled Representations for Robust Graph WatermarkingWWW
uses Learn disentangled (independent) parts of a graph's structure, embed them into a space, add watermarks to one part, then decode back to graph edits—avoiding mixed-up representations.
why it works It works because when you try to hide a watermark in a mixed-up graph representation, perturbations scatter the watermark everywhere and decoding becomes impossible. Pulling apart the structure first means you can control which part gets marked, then convert back to edits cleanly—like hiding a message in one wire of a bundle instead of tangling it through all wires.
Determinants and Effects of Buy Box Suppression on AmazonWWW
uses Measures whether product offers are removed from search ranking and tracks how this affects sales visibility and rank.
why it works The underlying truth is that rankings are causal—changing someone's visibility directly changes customer discovery. By tracking visibility before/after removal, you isolate the effect of one change and measure its real impact on sales metrics, proving causation not just correlation.
SJBP: A Platform to Launch a Novel Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models Based on Content's Spatial DistributionWWW
uses Spreads harmful content across spatial locations so filters see incomplete patterns separately, evading detection by safety systems.
why it works It works because most filters analyze text globally but miss relationships that span space. By distributing pieces across locations, the attack creates information that only exists when combined spatially—the filter sees fragments but never the unified malicious intent.
Unstructured to Structured: Building Knowledge Graphs from Documents for Web ApplicationsWWW
uses Extracts structured facts (entities, relations, events) from unstructured text using pattern recognition and learns to generalize across documents.
why it works It works because structured facts in text follow recurring linguistic patterns. By learning which patterns reliably signal which facts, you can then apply the same patterns to new unseen text, turning messy natural language into clean structured knowledge.
6th International Workshop on Computational Methods for Online Discourse Analysis (BeyondFacts'26)WWW
uses Analyzes online arguments and claims to detect stance, find reasoning patterns, and distinguish claims from disinformation using NLP methods.
why it works It works because arguments follow linguistic structures that reveal reasoning, and disinformation often uses distinctive language patterns. By learning which linguistic signals map to which argument properties, you can automatically detect them in new text—the patterns are learnable and transferable.
Truth with a Twist: The Rhetoric of Persuasion in Professional vs. Community-Authored Fact-ChecksWWW
uses Compares persuasion techniques used in community-written versus professional fact-checks to measure which ones actually influence crowd credibility ratings.
why it works It works because crowdsourced ratings reveal what actually persuades people. By comparing technique frequency across sources and correlating with helpfulness scores, you separate real persuasive effects from coincidence—showing what rhetoric patterns genuinely move judgments.
Grasp: Refining Semantic Graphs into Purified Knowledge for Cross-Modal CommunicationWWW
uses Minimize conditional mutual information to split representation into strongly related, weakly related, and task-irrelevant components.
why it works Mutual information measures dependence; minimizing it forces the model to break the signal into independent pieces. Irrelevant information becomes maximally independent from the task, so it gets squeezed out, leaving only what genuinely predicts the task.
Unveiling the Underground Phishing Ecosystem: A 12-Year Longitudinal Study of Deep and Dark Web ForumsWWW
uses Extract attack components from forum posts and track their availability over time to reveal emerging threats and attack methodologies.
why it works Components that suddenly become available signal new attack capability; components that disappear show declining risk. Observing longitudinal trends exposes cause-and-effect between ecosystem changes and real attacks.
Evaluating Trustworthiness in Reactive Web Architectures: A Structured Framework and Comparative AnalysisWWW
uses Measure recommender trustworthiness directly through human-centered metrics like agency and transparency, not through engagement proxies.
why it works Engagement (clicks, dwell time) is a side effect of trustworthiness, not a cause. Measuring engagement confuses correlation with causation; measuring trust and agency directly reveals what genuinely satisfies users in the long run.
Towards Rare Social Event Prediction via Mediator LearningWWW
uses Extract precursor events as mediators via information-theoretic routing, then model observed events, mediators, and rare events in hierarchical graph layers.
why it works Past events that carry the most information about rare events are the true precursors; routing by mutual information finds them automatically. Hierarchical layering lets the model learn what precursors matter and how they combine to trigger rare events.
Assessing the Reliability of Persona-Conditioned LLMs as Synthetic Survey RespondentsWWW
uses Tests whether conditioning a language model with demographic information improves its ability to mimic real survey respondents or instead distorts answers.
why it works It works because agreement with real data is the ground truth: by comparing model answers to actual respondents across thousands of cases, you can measure whether a technique like persona prompting creates accuracy or noise. Worse performance on underrepresented groups reveals redistribution of error, not overall improvement.
SGExplainer: Balanced Path-based Signed Graph Neural Network Explanation for Link Sign PredictionWWW
uses Identifies balanced paths through a network with both positive and negative connections to explain when the model predicts an edge will be good or bad.
why it works It works because in networks with positive and negative edges, a balanced path—one where positive and negative multiply to form a stable pattern—reveals why edges should exist. By generating balanced paths as explanations, you expose the causal structure the model learned: certain sequences of interactions naturally lead to positive or negative relationships.
The Algorithmic Self-Portrait:Deconstructing Memory in ChatGPTWWW
uses Analyze which memory entries an AI system infers about users, then alert when inferences reveal sensitive patterns.
why it works User inputs contain both direct statements and hidden clues to deeper traits; distinguishing stated facts from inferred psychology lets us see what the system learns and flag when inference chains accidentally expose sensitive information.
TGNN: Enhancing Pixel Tracking Detection via LLM-driven Annotation and GAT-powered Structural RepresentationWWW
uses Detect stealthy pixel trackers by modeling third-party associations on websites as a graph, then scoring which edges truly track users.
why it works Trackers survive because they hide in cross-site connections; modeling websites and third parties as a graph makes hidden patterns visible, and scoring edges separates tracking infrastructure from normal traffic.
Rethinking Implicit Hate Speech Detection: Focusing on Latent Hate Components via Dual-Process ArgumentationWWW
uses Find the actual hateful semantic units hidden in obfuscated text by mining candidates then debating their meaning, separating false surface cues from real harmful intent.
why it works Works because implicit hate uses misdirection — surface words seem innocent but underlying components carry the true message. Mining broadly then deliberating with reasoning separates noise from genuine signal, mimicking how humans detect what wasn't meant to be obvious.
Task-Aligned Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language ModelsWWW
uses Unlearn sensitive information by simultaneously pushing three separate goals: lower decision confidence on protected content, force refusals when asked about it, and suppress recall under both image and text prompts.
why it works Works because sensitive information is learned at multiple layers and gets triggered by different input types. Hitting it from three angles — decision making, generation, and recall — ensures no hidden path lets it leak out, and balances forgetting across all the behaviors the model learned.
Knowledge Graph Editing Model for Enhancing Recommendation SystemsWWW
uses Improve recommendations by denoising the knowledge graph to remove false associations, then reweight edges to highlight the ones that actually matter for the recommendation task.
