why it works Large models use enormous energy because every computation multiplies and sums thousands of numbers. Some numbers (salient values) matter far more than others. Spiking networks exploit this: they replace math with binary spikes and accumulation, which is cheap to compute and consume little power. By storing important values at full precision and rest as binary counts, the method keeps accuracy while dropping energy, because you only compute precisely what matters.
Expectation-Maximization Driven Contrastive Disentanglement for Generalized Category DiscoveryWWW
uses Discovers new categories by using a probabilistic model to soft-identify which samples belong to novel categories, then pulls similar samples close and pushes apart ambiguous ones.
why it works When a model learns only known categories, it biases everything toward them, so novel categories get misclassified. Using expectation-maximization to estimate which samples are likely novel (without requiring labels) lets the method assign soft probability to novelty. Then, contrasting samples within the same estimated category (pulling them close) while separating edge cases (pushing them apart) reinforces those assignments, so the model learns to separate categories it never saw.
llm-tuna - Hyperparameter Optimization for LLM InferenceWWW
uses Searches for optimal deployment settings (batch size, parallelism) by testing configurations intelligently across multiple hardware setups to maximize throughput.
why it works It works because the best settings depend on specific hardware, and intelligent sampling that learns from each trial gets to better configurations faster than random guessing, while parallelizing trials prevents exploring one bad path forever.
Marketing Hosting: From Fixed to Endogenous BudgetsWWW
uses Optimizes marketing spending when the budget itself depends on how well campaigns perform, learning the reinvestment rate that balances reward with risk of running out of money.
why it works It works because spending more when performance is good creates a feedback loop; tracking the coupling between rewards and remaining budget ensures you never make decisions that lead to certain ruin, unlike fixed-budget approaches.
MiniAMIE: Quick and Dirty Rule Mining on Knowledge GraphsWWW
uses Approximates which rules in knowledge graphs are most useful by testing quick estimates instead of exact measurements, speeding up mining.
why it works Testing every possible rule exhaustively is impossibly slow, so a good shortcut that ranks rules by approximate scores still finds the best ones while running fast. Missing some rules is acceptable as long as the best ones still rank highest.
Meteor: High-Performance Control Message Delivery for Large-Scale CloudsWWW
uses Routes control messages through either fast direct calls or slower queues, automatically switching between them based on which keeps delays lowest for each situation.
why it works Direct routes are fast but overload the control system; queues offload burden but add latency. Measuring which path is faster right now and switching between them minimizes delay, adapting to changing load without requiring a fixed choice.
Industrialized Deception: The Collateral Effects of LLM-Generated Misinformation on Digital EcosystemsWWW
uses Evaluates whether people can tell apart human news from AI-generated news, testing both detection and generation to understand how well AI fools readers and vice versa.
why it works Detection and generation capabilities form an arms race. By measuring how well humans spot AI news right now, you see which generation techniques still fool people and which defenses work, informing the next round of improvements on both sides.
Users Pay Twice: The Hidden Energy Cost of Web AdvertisingWWW
uses Measure CPU activity across millions of real web visits to estimate the energy cost that ads and tracking add to each page users browse.
why it works This works because energy is a physical, measurable quantity: by observing actual CPU time on actual devices with and without ads, you see the real cost, not a theoretical model. Scale and diversity of visits make the estimate robust.
Mind the Ambiguity: Aleatoric Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs for Safe Medical Question AnsweringWWW
uses Teaching a system to notice when a user's question has multiple meanings and ask for clarification, by detecting ambiguity directly from the system's internal thought-patterns.
why it works It works because ambiguity leaves a measurable fingerprint in how the system computes—if you learn to read that fingerprint early (from hidden computation stages) you can ask for help before giving a wrong answer, avoiding the error entirely.
Coarse-Fine: A Novel VPA Strategy for Boosting Resource Utilization of Transient Offline TasksWWW
uses Adjusting computer resource requests for tasks by combining cluster-wide trends with sliding-window patterns specific to each task's recent history.
why it works It works because tasks are not random—they show repeatable seasonal patterns (time of day, day of week) that a sliding window captures, while the broad cluster trend prevents over-fitting to one task's quirks. Together they predict what each task actually needs next.
LaTune: Lightweight and Adaptive Configuration Tuning for LLM Inference on Edge DevicesWWW
uses Find which runtime settings matter most, reuse successful settings from past tuning runs, then quickly pick the best live configuration based on what system resources are available right now.
why it works It works because not all settings change performance equally—focusing on the sensitive ones saves time. Reusing old successful solutions speeds up the search, and because device resources shift during execution, dynamic adjustment ensures robustness without full re-tuning.
Ethical Decision-Making under Moral UncertaintyWWW
uses Balance competing moral frameworks by assigning weights to each ethical principle, learn which principles work best by trying arms, and dynamically adjust weights based on observed outcomes.
why it works It works because you never know which ethical rule is right, so you explore all of them. Assigning them weights lets you hedge between contradictory principles, and learning which bets paid off lets you gradually shift weight toward the most reliable ones.
Optimizing Multi-Turn Interactive Recommendation Agents via Generative Intrinsic MotivationWWW
uses The system learns to act by assigning rewards based on three human drives (autonomy, competence, relatedness), then improves choices by descending toward better behavior.
why it works These three drives match how humans actually learn and stay motivated. Rewarding actions that feed each drive naturally guides the agent toward both competent behavior and smart exploration, and the direction-descent process guarantees steady improvement.
Bridging Expert Reasoning and LLM Detection: A Knowledge-Driven Framework for Malicious PackagesWWW
uses The detector retrieves similar dangerous code examples from a knowledge base, then uses reasoning to assess whether new code's purpose matches its behavior.
why it works Malicious code follows patterns. By comparing new code against past harmful examples, you inherit centuries of expert judgment compressed into those examples. If the new code matches a dangerous pattern's shape, the odds it is dangerous rise sharply.
AHBid: An Adaptable Hierarchical Bidding Framework for Cross-Channel AdvertisingWWW
uses The system plans budget allocation across ad channels by sampling many plausible allocation paths from past patterns, then refining them in real-time as new outcomes arrive.
why it works Past budgets and outcomes show which allocations worked. Sampling from that distribution generates good starting guesses for today. Real-time refinement adjusts guesses when today's market differs, avoiding both rigid pre-planned budgets and algorithms that forget yesterday's lessons.
SLFM: Semi-Supervised Local Community Detection Based on Hyperbolic Flow MatchingWWW
uses The system finds a community around a seed user by learning a lists of numbers field that smoothly transforms a generic distribution into the target community's shape in curved space, starting from a refined seed.
why it works Curved space geometry captures hierarchy in networks; radius encodes depth and angle encodes type. Learning to flow between distributions in this space lets you generate new community members that respect both local geometry and the anchor points, avoiding seed misguidence.
CytoCrowd: A Multi-Annotator Benchmark Dataset for Cytology Image AnalysisWWW
uses Aggregate labels from multiple pathologists into a single quality judgment about each cell.
why it works When experts disagree, taking a weighted average of their judgments exploits the fact that real signals align across independent observers, while random mistakes cancel out. Gold-standard ground truth confirms which averaged labels capture the true pattern.
Bandits, LLMs, and Agentic WebWWW
uses An AI agent chooses actions by treating each option as an arm in a bandit; it learns which choices earn rewards, explores uncertain ones, and converges to the best strategies.
why it works Exploration-exploitation is a fundamental trade-off: pure exploitation locks in what seems best now, but misses discovery; pure exploration wastes time. Bandit algorithms balance the two by measuring uncertainty in each option and skewing effort toward high-reward AND uncertain choices. This provably converges to optimal action selection in the long run.
G-SEIR: A Graph-Enhanced Epidemic Forecasting System for Dengue InterventionWWW
uses Predict future dengue cases by running a learned disease-spread simulator on a spatio-temporal network, with parameters optimized to match past outbreak data.
why it works Disease spreads by contact along geographic networks; the SEIR model captures this flow (susceptible to exposed to infected to recovered). By tuning the spread rates on historical data, the simulator learns the true pace of transmission in this region, so running it forward projects realistic futures.
Multilingual Reference Need Assessment System for WikipediaWWW
uses Trains a model on ten languages simultaneously to spot Wikipedia claims that lack citations, balancing accuracy against the cost to run it at production scale.
why it works It works because Wikipedia editors work across languages and edit patterns are similar everywhere; training together means rare signals in one language strengthen the model for others. Balancing accuracy and cost reveals that you don't need perfection if you catch the highest-risk claims reliably.
Benchmarking Temporal Web3 Intelligence: Lessons from the FinSurvival 2025 ChallengeWWW
uses Predict user transitions and survival in a blockchain platform using 16 survival prediction tasks on 21.8 million transactions, capturing temporal censoring and non-stationary patterns.
why it works This works because survival tasks directly model what matters in blockchain ecosystems: whether a user stays active or churns, accounting for the fact that some users drop out (censored) and market conditions shift over time. Real temporal data with these properties is rarer than simpler benchmarks, so learning robust methods on it transfers to other Web domains where behavior also censors and drifts. Building a shared benchmark lets researchers compete on same ground, improving generality.
FSDI: Frequency-Shaped Diffusion For Time-Series ImputationWWW
uses Replaces uniform noise scheduling with frequency-specific noise amounts matched to how energy is actually distributed across the frequency spectrum of time series data.
why it works It works because real signals concentrate their power unevenly across frequencies—some bands have more signal, others mostly noise. By adding less noise to high-energy bands and more to low-energy ones, you preserve the natural structure. This makes it easier for the model to recover the true signal during reconstruction.
EdgeGen: Efficient LLM-Empowered Model Generation with Quantization-Aware NASWWW
uses Searches for neural architectures that perform well even after compression, by numeric fingerprints quantization into the search space and using tree-based random sampling to explore efficiently.
why it works Standard architecture search finds models that are small but not well-designed for compression. By quantizing models during search, you discover architectures that compress well. Tree-based sampling with many parallel workers explores the huge space of models and quantizations without exhaustive evaluation.
AC$2$L-GAD: Active Counterfactual Contrastive Learning for Graph Anomaly DetectionWWW
uses Learns which pairs of network nodes are truly anomalies by comparing how similar they are and what's unusual about them.
why it works Comparing similar things reveals anomalies because normal nodes cluster together in their patterns, while anomalies sit alone. Weighting the hard-to-distinguish pairs heavily forces the method to get those right.
BANCO: Drift-Aware Batched Bandits for Adaptive Proximity Graph PruningWWW
uses Tries different strategies for removing graph edges and learns which works best as the data distribution changes over time.
why it works It works because you can try strategies in small batches, measure which reduces error most, and adapt when data shifts. Regular sampling and averaging helps estimate which strategy is truly best.
Reinforcement Learning with Verbalized Probabilities for LLM ClassificationWWW
uses Teach the language model to output word-based probability scores by rewarding it with feedback from expert math-based models trained on tabular data.
why it works Expert models encode reliable ordering and confidence in probabilities. When you reward the language model for matching those signals, it learns to produce calibrated confidence estimates. Dense, fine-grained rewards guide learning much faster than simple right-or-wrong signals.
Empowering LLMs for Structure-Based Drug Design via Exploration-Augmented Latent InferenceWWW
uses Guides a language model to explore chemical space by scoring candidate molecules and focusing on unexplored regions to avoid missing better designs.
why it works Unexplored regions likely contain better molecules than thoroughly searched areas. Balancing exploration vs refinement avoids local traps; scoring (binding affinity) directs the search toward useful molecules.
Curiosity Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Mobile AgentsWWW
uses The agent learns to recognize when it lacks knowledge and retrieves documentation to fill gaps before acting.
why it works Uncertainty measured by curiosity score reveals exactly when and what external knowledge helps; targeted retrieval beats pre-loading all facts.
Zelda: Feedback-driven Closed-box Fuzzing for Identifying Web Application VulnerabilitiesWWW
uses The fuzzer generates random web inputs, learns from response patterns to guide exploration, and identifies bugs.
why it works Responses leak information about internal code paths; sampling smartly based on what responses reveal finds more paths than random tries.
Fairness at a Glance: Can We Audit Model Fairness Before Training Completes?WWW
uses Predicts whether a model will meet fairness requirements by examining early training behavior before training completes.
why it works It works because fairness trajectories are stable—once training starts, the direction and speed of change remain predictable. If fairness improves early, it keeps improving. This predictability lets you stop unfair models early without waiting for full training, saving computation.
Toward Generalized Web Agent Training: A Deep Dive into Entropy-Balanced Reinforcement LearningWWW
uses Monitor exploration randomness in rollouts and policy updates to balance branch sampling budget and penalize consecutive high-how much surprise actions that cause training collapse.
why it works Randomness drives exploration and discovers good actions, but too much causes the model to jump erratically. Monitoring how much surprise pre-emptively detects when exploration goes excessive and local penalties prevent cascading failures from high-how much surprise decisions.
Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) Dataset Generator Framework for IoT EnvironmentsWWW
uses Simulate diverse model families across multiple real datasets and distribution settings to generate benchmark instances for evaluating service selection.
why it works Testing selection strategies on many realistic scenarios reveals which generalizes best. Averaging performance across diverse conditions filters out luck; if a strategy wins on most scenarios, it has discovered something robust.
Energy-Efficient Training-Free Zero-Inflation Correction for Rainfall Forecasting with Time-Series Foundation ModelsWWW
uses Fix rainfall forecasts by tuning when to predict rain versus no rain using historical occurrence rates and extreme-value adjustment.
why it works Models trained on average values miss the structural truth that rain is rare; matching empirical statistics of zeros and extreme values aligns predictions to reality without retraining, because the model's hidden knowledge already captures the right patterns.
Aligning Query Rewriting with Human Cognition and Preference in E-Commerce SearchWWW
uses Diagnoses rewriting problems in search queries, then learns human-like fixes through supervised training and preference-aligned beam search ranking.
why it works It works because humans rewrite queries systematically: certain problems map to certain fixes. Learning this mapping directly from human examples, then using ranked search to pick rewrites that match both human and retrieval-system preferences, produces more natural and effective query corrections.
HomeRun: Performing Curveball Trades quasi in Streaming for Fast Null Modeling of Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Binary MatricesWWW
uses Quickly shuffle network structures by sampling which pairs to swap, processing data almost in one pass without repeatedly scanning.
why it works Reservoir sampling lets you pick random swaps without knowing how many total options exist; framing swaps as sampling problems means you compute only what you absolutely need, cutting passes from multiple down to one.
BARouter: A Budget-adaptive Online Large Language Model Router FrameworkWWW
uses Dynamically assign the computation budget to each query based on quality estimates and remaining budget, minimizing total regret.
why it works It works because allocating more budget where quality matters most and less where queries are simple balances response quality against total cost; sublinear regret means the allocation strategy learns to spread resources optimally over time.
PMIScore: An Unsupervised Approach to Quantify Dialogue EngagementWWW
uses Measures how much a response depends on conversation history using information theory to quantify engagement.
why it works It works because coherent, engaging conversations have responses that naturally follow from context. When responses tightly depend on history, the conversation shows real engagement rather than random replies.
Tail-Aware Data Augmentation for Long-Tail Sequential RecommendationWWW
uses Boost recommendations for unpopular items and users by augmenting their sequences with similar items while keeping popular items performing well.
why it works Tail items suffer from sparse data—few users buy them. By augmenting their sequences with related items that co-occur, you provide the model more signal without creating fake interactions. Selective substitution and insertion preserve head performance because the method only adds synthetic data where sparsity hurts most.
Urban Traffic Network Layout Optimization with Guided Discrete Diffusion ModelsWSDM
uses Design better traffic layouts by training a model to gradually build valid road networks from noise, guided by predictions of how each layout performs.
why it works It works because gradual building respects real constraints (roads must connect, follow zones) at each step, while the performance model steers toward layouts that reduce congestion. This outperforms random search in huge spaces.
TaxoDiff: Improving Taxonomy Completion with Diffusion Guided Dynamic Negative SamplingWSDM
uses Generate increasingly difficult negative examples using diffusion to improve the ranking model, rather than using random negatives.
why it works It works because random negatives are too easy: the model learns to distinguish obvious non-fits and never builds strong discrimination. Progressively harder negatives force the model to refine its distinctions, learning subtle features that separate close calls, leading to better taxonomy predictions.
Mixture of Adaptive Retrieval Experts for Veracity Assessment in the Human–LLM Mixed Generation ParadigmWSDM
uses Dynamically choose whether to retrieve evidence and how much, using multiple retrieval experts balanced by learning which source generated each piece of content.
why it works AI language systems-generated and human-written false information have different patterns — what looks like a lie in one context looks normal in another. Rather than using one retrieval strategy for everything, training multiple experts and letting the source characteristics determine which expert to use adapts to what actually needs to be verified.
Stealing Black-box Hyperdimensional Computing Models Without DataWSDM
uses Generate synthetic data through noise and augmentation, then train a copy that mimics a black-box model's outputs.
why it works You can't steal a model directly, but you can teach a new model to behave identically by observing outputs on many inputs. Since the model always gives the same output for the same input, a well-trained copy becomes functionally identical even without seeing the internals.
Counteracting the Delayed Conversions in OCPC with Survival AnalysisWSDM
uses Predicts when clicks convert to purchases by modeling time-to-conversion as a survival curve, accounting for delays between user action and actual purchase.
why it works It works because conversion times are not random—they follow systematic patterns based on user type, item, and context. By modeling what fraction convert by each time point, you uncover these hidden delays and stop underestimating the true cost per conversion.
CATS: Cluster-Aware Thompson Sampling for Negative Mining in Sequential RecommendationSIGIR
uses Sample training examples adaptively by clustering items, then grab negatives from nearby clusters (high risk of false negatives) less as training goes on, and far clusters (true hard cases) more.
why it works Items in the same cluster look similar, so they could easily be mislabeled as 'not liked'. By sampling them less over time, you reduce false negatives. Far clusters are genuinely different, so negatives there are trustworthy.
Decision-Theoretic Stopping Rules for Document ScreeningSIGIR
uses Decide when to stop reviewing search results by computing the expected benefit of finding one more relevant item versus the cost of reviewing it.
why it works At some point, the next document is unlikely to be relevant enough to justify the cost of reading it. Expected value tells you exactly when that crossover happens.
R3Check: Reinforcement Learning for Iterative Retrieval and Structured Reasoning in Complex Fact CheckingSIGIR
uses Iteratively retrieve evidence and reason over it to check facts, using reinforcement learning that rewards correct final verdicts and structured reasoning format.
why it works It works because fact-checking has structure—you must gather evidence before judging. Rewarding both format compliance and correctness teaches the model to build reasoning chains that gather relevant evidence step-by-step, avoiding hallucination.
SynDiSC: High-Quality Tabular Data Synthesis with Distributional and Semantic ConsistencySIGIR
uses Generates synthetic tabular data that preserves both the statistics of the original data and the logical relationships between fields.
why it works It works because real data has structure; enforcing that synthetic samples obey the same conditional rules as the original makes them realistic and usable for downstream tasks.
Generative Auto-Bidding with Unified Modeling and ExplorationSIGIR
uses Learn expected future value of bids using a score function, generate candidate bids by sampling from a learned bid distribution, and reweight samples by a learned fallback policy to reduce financial risk.
why it works It works because you're balancing exploration (trying new bid levels) with safety (falling back to known-good policies when learning is uncertain). The score function guides exploration toward higher returns, while the fallback prevents catastrophic bids.
Beyond Top-e: Simulation-Based Interactive Evaluation for Query SuggestionsSIGIR
uses Simulate how users select query suggestions by training a model to predict selection based on relevance to search intent; use simulated selection to evaluate suggestion quality.
why it works It works because real users follow a predictable decision process: they choose suggestions aligned with what they're searching for. A model trained on real selection patterns can approximate future user behavior, enabling offline evaluation that captures the interactive dynamics of actual query refinement.
F2-Gen: An Open-Source Web Platform for Scenario-Driven Financial Fraud Data SimulationSIGIR
uses Generate synthetic financial transaction data and fraud patterns configured by scenario parameters; create realistic tabular and graph data for anomaly detection research.
why it works It works because fraud detection models need diverse examples to learn patterns, but real bank data is locked away. Synthetic data generated from known fraud scenarios (money mule, structuring, etc.) provides labeled examples that capture the essential statistical signatures of real fraud without exposing private transactions.
Multilingual and Domain-Agnostic Tip-of-the-Tongue Query Generation for Simulated EvaluationSIGIR
uses Generate tip-of-the-tongue queries across four languages by simulating user memory recall from documents; validate simulated queries against real user search behavior.
why it works It works because tip-of-the-tongue queries follow patterns: users remember fragments of meaning, not exact wording. A model trained on that pattern and validated against real users can generate synthetic queries that behave like human queries, enabling multilingual benchmark construction without extensive human search logs.
Partial Label Learning-Inspired Denoising Implicit Feedback for RecommendationSIGIR
uses Treat noisy implicit feedback as having multiple possible labels, then learn to disambiguate which feedback is true signal versus noise.
why it works It works because clicks and views are genuinely ambiguous—a click might be a misclick or an unsatisfactory item. By modeling the ambiguity explicitly as a set of possible labels rather than forcing a hard choice, the model learns to recognize which signals are reliable while handling uncertainty gracefully.
Query-Aware Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented GenerationSIGIR
uses Predict how many search results a specific query needs to answer properly, then dynamically fetch that many instead of always using the same top-k number.
why it works Queries vary in complexity and answer diversity. Simple queries need few results; complex ones need more. If you always fetch the same number, simple queries get irrelevant noise (hurting answers) and complex ones get incomplete evidence. Learning what each query needs avoids both problems.
SocialDropout: Dynamic Agent Dropout for Social SimulationSIGIR
uses Learn which agents to include in each simulation round by assigning adaptive importance weights that minimize computational cost while preserving interaction intensity.
why it works Not all agents are equally informative at every step. By learning which ones drive the dynamics and sampling them preferentially, you cut computation without losing the emergent social behavior.
Why Knowledge Distillation Fails to Scale in Neural RetrievalSIGIR
uses When a large student model learns from a smaller teacher model, the teacher's capacity limits how much the student can learn; a larger teacher lets the larger student actually improve.
why it works It works because the student can only learn patterns that the teacher can express; if the teacher is too small to capture all the patterns a large model could use, the teacher becomes a bottleneck and the student stops improving even if it has more capacity to learn.
How Trendyol Enables Trustworthy A/B Testing at E-Commerce Scale Through Integrated Statistical MethodologiesSIGIR
uses Balance user groups in A/B tests and monitor how confident each result is, stopping early when you have enough signal to declare a winner.
why it works It works because random assignment isn't enough—user populations have hidden structure. By matching similar users across groups you reduce noise, and by tracking power (confidence) alongside significance you catch weak signals before declaring victory. This catches false wins early.
LLM-Informed Bayesian Content Exploration in Ultra-Recency RecommendationSIGIR
uses A language model reads new content and gives a confidence score for quality before any user sees it; this score seeds exploration so the system efficiently allocates early views.
why it works Brand-new content has zero user data. A language model can judge quality and appeal from the content itself, alone—reading text and images like a human would. Using this as a starting belief (a Bayesian starting guess) lets the system explore confidently with early users, guided by semantic judgment rather than blind chance. As real user data arrives, it updates the belief.
Variance Reduction for Heavy-Tailed Monetization Metrics in Ranking Experiments via Post-StratificationSIGIR
uses Reduce the variability in revenue metrics by grouping similar users and subtracting out their known pre-experiment differences.
why it works It works because revenue data has extreme outliers that wash out real effects. By separating users into strata with similar earning potential and measuring within each group, you amplify the true signal and ignore the noise from random variation in who happens to be in your test group.
As It Was: Aligning LLM Search Evaluation with Historical User PreferencesSIGIR
uses Strengthen relevance judgments by comparing each result to a record of how users actually clicked on similar queries and results before.
why it works It works because real user behavior is ground truth for what relevance means in context. Grounding judgments in this empirical history resolves ambiguity more reliably than reasoning alone, especially on edge cases where multiple answers seem plausible.
C3Flow: SIMD-Style Concurrent Claude Code Workflow for Scaling Deep ResearchSIGIR
uses Run many agent instances in parallel on similar tasks and measure how many pass, then optimize routing across different models to improve success rates.
why it works It works because parallel runs on identical tasks reveal whether improvements come from the approach or chance, and routing to the best model for each step finds the steepest improvement path without running all models every time.
85 papers

Focusing on what's relevant

Not every part of an input matters equally, so the system learns to put its weight on the pieces relevant to the moment and quietly ignore the rest.

Why it works — the principle

It works because in most inputs the useful signal is sparse — a few words, a few past actions carry the meaning — so a method that learns to weight those few heavily and downplay the rest keeps the signal and throws away the noise, doing far more with the same data.

Structure-Semantic Synergized Deep Contrastive Graph ClusteringWWW
uses Clusters graph nodes by contrasting reliable structural neighbors against hard negatives, weighted by how much each node's connections and cross-view agreement reveal its true category.
why it works When you force a model to say 'this structure is similar to good examples and different from bad ones', it learns to recognize true patterns. Weighting by confidence focuses learning on the clearest cases, letting genuine signals drown out noise.
pFedDKS: Detached Knowledge Sharing for Personalized Federated LearningWWW
uses Learn a shared feature processor that each client can customize locally, by identifying which layers should be global and which should be personal.
why it works Sharing everything causes clients' personal needs to get averaged out. Keeping some layers local lets each client's unique features shine through. The math works because the theory of neural collapse shows that too much averaging at the feature level hurts personalization, while partial sharing balances shared knowledge and individual needs.
BeeQoS: A Cloud-Native QoS System for Adaptive and Scalable Multi-Priority Bandwidth GuaranteesWWW
uses Dynamically measure real-time flow demand and reallocate bandwidth weights across priority tiers, adjusting per-packet shaping rules to minimize latency violations.
why it works Bandwidth allocation is a resource-rationing problem: giving more to high-priority flows reduces their wait time exponentially more than taking it from low-priority flows hurts theirs. By sensing demand and adapting weights continuously, you maximize the reduction in worst-case latency.
ToxiTwitch: Toward Emote-Aware Hybrid Moderation for Live Streaming PlatformsWWW
uses Generate feature representations of both text and emotes, then train a classifier that scores which combinations indicate toxic behavior.
why it works Toxic meaning depends on context and emoji intent, which text classifiers alone miss. Extracting features from both channels separately lets the learner discover which emote-text pairs signal toxicity, and weighting their joint signal is more robust than text alone because it captures the full intent.
Facilitating Generative Retrieval with Logical Denoising for Interpretable Conversational SearchWWW
uses Generate relevant documents for conversational search by denoising conversation context with logic, then learning which starting guess turns matter most for each turn.
why it works Not all conversation history helps equally; weighting turns by logical coherence and relevance ensures the model attends to clarifying context while ignoring off-topic digressions.
Responsible Prompting on the Web: Governance, Mini-Evaluation, and Readiness with ChatGPTWWW
uses Prompting uses structured instructions and examples to guide what the model generates, filtering risky outputs before deployment.
why it works Text generation learns statistical patterns from training data; explicit instructions and examples steer that learned pattern-matching toward safe, useful outputs.
ToolBox-RL: Learning to Generalize Tool Use Across Massive RepositoriesWWW
uses Learn which tools best match user intent by optimizing a reward signal from successful tool calls on diverse queries.
why it works Tool selection is a ranking problem; trial-and-error with reward feedback discovers which features of a query predict tool match. Reinforcement learning works because success/failure is directly observable.
HAAF: Hierarchical Adaptation and Alignment of Foundation Models for Few-Shot Pathology Anomaly DetectionWWW
uses A cross-level mechanism first grounds text descriptions in visual context, then uses those descriptions to focus the visual encoder on anomalous regions.
why it works It works because fine-grained defects require top-down linguistic guidance combined with bottom-up visual focus; by enforcing sequential alignment where vision informs text and text refocuses vision, the model grounds semantics in diagnostic reality rather than treating modalities independently.
Dual-level Reweighting for Positive-Unlabeled Graph ClassificationWWW
uses Reweight graph substructures at two levels—hop-level to focus on informative patterns, graph-level to suppress ambiguous unlabeled examples—for classification with only positive and unlabeled data.
why it works It works because without negative labels, the model must infer what looks wrong by finding patterns unique to positive examples. Dual reweighting focuses focus: first on the subgraph parts that discriminate, then on confident examples, shrinking the space of noise.
RAFed: Responsive Augmentation and Approximate Update Method for Federated Learning with Non-IID DataWWW
uses Learn which data transformations help each client by tuning a policy that predicts how a transformation will help unseen local data, then apply personalized transformations to each client separately.
why it works Blind transformations fail because each client's data is different; by estimating the policy on each client's own data without sending it, you can predict what will help, and personalizing per-client accounts for their unique quirks without sharing sensitive information.
AdaQE-CG: Adaptive Query Expansion for Web-Scale Generative AI Model and Data Card GenerationWWW
uses Build model and data documentation cards by iteratively refining extraction queries to find richer information from papers, then filling gaps by borrowing relevant content from similar existing cards.
why it works Static queries miss information because papers vary in structure; iterative refinement discovers what matters for each paper, and borrowing from semantically similar cards fills gaps without having to re-extract everything, reusing what you already learned.
Amortized Predictability-aware Training Framework for Time Series Forecasting and ClassificationWWW
uses Score each time-series sample by how predictable it is, weight the loss penalty higher for harder-to-learn samples, and refine this weighting across training iterations.
why it works It works because focusing more compute on difficult examples improves the model's grasp of edge cases without abandoning them entirely. Noisy or unusual samples that mislead learning get lower weight at first, then gradually higher weight as the main model strengthens, preventing collapse into poor local solutions.
Privacy-Friendly Adaptation of Vision Transformers for Communication and Latency-Efficient Private InferenceWWW
uses Reduce the cost of secure computation for image analysis models by reusing feature representations across similar layers, approximating expensive components with cheaper stand-ins that stay accurate enough.
why it works It works because secure multi-party computation is expensive—every operation requires coordination—so reusing results saves rounds of communication. Approximation works because the model can tolerate small errors in expensive layers as long as the approximation is smooth and consistent; you're trading a tiny accuracy dip for huge latency savings.
Prism: Towards Lowering User Cognitive Load in LLMs via Complex Intent UnderstandingWWW
uses Break down ambiguous user goals into logical dependencies, then ask clarifying questions in an order that respects those dependencies.
why it works It works because human intent is hierarchical: some questions must be answered before others make sense. By respecting logical order instead of asking randomly, you reduce cognitive load and get better answers faster, because each question builds on starting guess clarity.
SaGD: A Node-Level Differentially Private Graph Learning Framework with Sensitivity-Aware Gradient DescentWWW
uses Weight the connections between users based on graph structure to control how much changing one user's data can shift the model.
why it works In graphs, changing one node's data can propagate through connections to affect distant predictions. Weighting edges to bound this propagation lets you prove how much noise is needed to hide individual changes, without cutting edges.
FedBridge: Accelerating Edge-Assisted Federated Learning for Model-Heterogeneous ClientsWWW
uses Blend knowledge from multiple differently-shaped models through a shared fusion model on each edge server, using contrastive learning to align each fusion model with the global consensus.
why it works Model-heterogeneous clients can't share weights directly; a fusion model learned via distillation extracts the useful knowledge from each architecture-specific model, translating it to a common representation. Contrastive learning (pulling fusion raw scores close to global raw scores, pushing away others) ensures the fusion captures only generalizable insights, not client-specific noise.
CIDC: Cluster Identification-Guided Dual Correction for Robust Short Text ClusteringWWW
uses Guesses which category each cluster should represent, then corrects its own training labels whenever samples disagree with their cluster's category, re-centering clusters on reliable examples.
why it works It works because noisy pseudo-labels steer learning in circles; by identifying the single most likely true category for each cluster, you can detect and fix labels that contradict the cluster's true identity. Fixing the worst labels each iteration ensures the model converges on semantically coherent groups.
Multi-field Balance-aware Calibration of Predictions in Online AdvertisingWWW
uses Balance prediction errors across different ad targeting fields by finding the best mix of weights that minimizes errors simultaneously on all fields—never perfect on one but good on all.
why it works It works because different fields have different error patterns; a single global fix helps some users but harms others. Finding the non-dominated middle ground (Pareto frontier) ensures no field gets systematically cheated, and forces honest trade-offs rather than hiding bias in one direction.
SAMPLE: A Spatial/Channel-wise Attention GCN with MLP and Periodic Linear Encoding for Land Boundary Demarcation SystemWWW
uses Predict fieldwork duration for land surveying by weighting spatial and tabular information differently per location, using periodic patterns and network-of-connections to capture what matters locally.
why it works It works because different locations have different terrain types and task difficulties; allowing spatial focus to weight information per location captures local variation. Periodic encoding captures cyclical workload patterns, and network connections let similar locations help each other's predictions.
FedAKD: Federated Adaptive Knowledge Distillation via Global Knowledge Calibration and DecouplingWWW
uses Calibrate distilled knowledge by weighting underrepresented classes more heavily on each local device.
why it works Works because weighting amplifies the global knowledge for rare classes, preventing local data imbalance from drowning out what the global model learned about minority groups.
Not All Information Brings Benefits: Personalization-Driven Agent Debate for Conversational RecommendationWWW
uses For conversational recommendations, debate which historical conversations help and which hurt the current decision, then weight only the helpful ones into the preference model.
why it works It works because old conversations can mislead—a debate mechanism identifies which past exchanges are truly relevant to today's intent versus which are noise; selective weighting then amplifies signal and mutes interference.
HAUTE: Harmonizing Action Units with Temporal-contextual Embeddings for Deepfake DetectionWWW
uses Detects deepfakes by learning temporal patterns in facial muscle movements and weighting which temporal and semantic features matter most for spotting synthesis artifacts.
why it works It works because real faces have consistent muscle coordination over time; deepfakes synthesize inconsistently. Weighting relevant features heavily focuses on exactly where synthesis fails.
MessageShift: Fine-Grained Data Augmentation for Graph Neural NetworksWWW
uses Strengthens systems that learn from examples for graphs by slightly shifting messages toward or away from neighbors—sharpening distinctive ones and softening noisy ones—during learning.
why it works It works because messages carrying strong unique signals should be amplified and noise suppressed. Contextual shifting toward neighbors for similar messages smooths noise; away for divergent ones sharpens.
Dynamic Multi-period Experts for Online Time Series ForecastingWWW
uses Maintain multiple expert models, each specialized to a historical periodic pattern; dynamically route each forecast to the expert whose pattern best matches the current condition, or to a stable baseline if no pattern matches.
why it works Time series often repeat seasonal cycles and weekly patterns. Experts trained on past cycles recognize and forecast their own pattern well. When a genuinely new pattern arrives, no expert matches; routing to a stable baseline prevents experts from extrapolating wrongly. Dynamic selection exploits repetition without being fooled by novelty.
Unveiling and Simulating Short-Video Addiction Behaviors via Economic Addiction TheoryWWW
uses Models short-video addiction by learning personalized patterns from behavioral data, then weights individual user trajectories to train a simulator that predicts how users consume content.
why it works It works because addiction follows economic principles—people trade off short-term reward against long-term cost—and behavioral data encodes these tradeoffs implicitly; weighting by individual differences captures why some users escalate while others self-regulate.
Lurkers, Interactors, Creators: Modeling Behavioral and Ideological Diversity on XWWW
uses Segments social media users into behavioral profiles by clustering session-level activity patterns, then weights groups by engagement style to explain differences in content exposure.
why it works It works because each user type—lurkers, creators, interactors—prioritizes different signals (visibility, participation, curation), so their information environments diverge; clustering users by behavior, then weighting by group priorities, reveals why the same platform shows different content to different types.
Not All Candidates are Created Equal: A Heterogeneity-Aware Approach to Pre-ranking in Recommender SystemsWWW
uses Separates easy and hard items to rank, uses simple models for easy ones and stronger models for hard ones, balancing ranking accuracy with computational cost.
why it works Hard items teach the model more; easy items teach little but cost the same to process. By spending budget where you learn most (on hard cases) and skipping hard processing on easy cases, you reach the same accuracy faster. Routing samples intelligently instead of treating all equally reduces wasted computation.
Unlocking the Multilingual Long-Tail Web: A Fused Macro-Micro Framework for Scalable Content AnalysisWWW
uses Tunes a language model by injecting language structure hints early, then uses error signals to dynamically adjust what the model learns at each training step.
why it works Language has hidden structure (word order, grammar rules) that constrains meaning; injecting these patterns early creates a robust foundation. Feedback-guided curriculum focuses on hard examples, avoiding wasted effort on easy ones.
Unveiling Backdoor Propagation in Graphs: Neuron-Centric Defense MechanismsWWW
uses Identify which internal features get activated by backdoor triggers, then unlearn and recover those features to remove poisoned behaviors.
why it works Poisoned models work because backdoor triggers exploit specific internal pathways. Identifying which internal features activate tells you the attack's mechanism. Unlearning those features removes the attack's grip without erasing all learning. Restoring clean versions of those features recovers the model's ability to behave honestly.
Revisiting IPS-based Algorithms for Off-Policy Evaluation of Contextual BanditsWWW
uses Evaluates whether a recommendation policy is good by reweighting historical logs so they represent what would have happened if the new policy had been used, using probability scores to correct for the original policy's choices.
why it works It works because logged data only shows actions the old policy took, but you need to know how people would have responded to the new policy. Inverse propensity weighting corrects for bias by up-weighting rare actions the new policy favors and down-weighting common actions it avoids, making the log representative of the counterfactual.
Weighted Graph Clustering via Scale Contraction and Graph Structure LearningWWW
uses Shrink a weighted graph by removing unimportant nodes, then use learned weights to soften noisy edges so they matter less in clustering.
why it works It works because not all edges carry clustering signal—some are just noise. By learning which edges to trust (high weight) and which to ignore (low weight) while also removing nodes that don't help clusters form, you concentrate the signal and reduce memory. Comparing which nodes form tight clusters guides you on what to keep.
CCAF: Coarse-to-fine Cross-Modal Alignment and Fusion for Multimodal Sentiment AnalysisWWW
uses Align sentiment clues across text, image, and audio both globally and locally, fuse them with adaptive gates, then use learned sentiment prototypes to remove redundant information.
why it works It works because sentiment hides in fine details (a raised eyebrow matters) and overall tone (the whole is happier than parts suggest). Aligning both scales separately lets you catch what each modality contributes. Prototypes are like ideal sentiment templates—comparing to them tells you which aligned details are redundant noise versus new meaning.
SAGE-RAI: Design Patterns for Transparent RAG SystemsWWW
uses Shows users which sources a knowledge-retrieval system read before generating answers, making its reasoning transparent and verifiable.
why it works It works because trust requires traceability. When users see the sources, they can verify the reasoning independently. Transparency acts as a built-in fact-check—any hallucination or misinterpretation becomes visible, and good reasoning becomes independently confirmable.
Measuring and Enhancing Human Value Alignment in Zero-Shot Document-Level Claim ExtractionWWW
uses Extracts key claims from long documents by learning which claim types experts value using their annotations as examples.
why it works It works because expert annotations reveal exactly what claim properties matter—importance, factuality, relevance. By learning from those examples, the system learns the implicit quality criteria. Models trained on curated examples learn what makes a claim worth extracting.
WinFLoRA: Incentivizing Client-Adaptive Aggregation in Federated LoRA under Privacy HeterogeneityWWW
uses Weights updates from each client based on estimated noise levels to improve a shared language model while respecting each client's privacy choices.
why it works It works because you can estimate the noise level in an update by observing its properties, then reward low-noise contributions with higher influence on the final model. Focusing on cleaner updates automatically improves overall accuracy since better information outweighs corrupted information in any combination.
FairFS: Addressing Deep Feature Selection Biases for Recommender SystemWWW
uses Measures which input features matter most to a recommendation model by correcting for biases that cause rankings to depend on only some layers, samples, or slope directions.
why it works It works because importance should reflect all the model's layers equally, not just the ones that happen to have large slope. By keeping it simple importance estimates across all layers and using a baseline near the decision boundary, you measure how much each feature truly matters to the final prediction, not an artifact of how the model is structured.
Delayed Feedback Modeling for Post-Click Gross Merchandise Volume Prediction: Benchmark, Insights and ApproachesWWW
uses Predict total purchase spending after a click by routing examples through separate models for single-purchase and repeat-purchase paths, with adaptive target calibration to handle incomplete labels arriving over time.
why it works Works because repeat buyers and one-time buyers follow different spending patterns, so a shared model would average them out incorrectly. Separate paths let each learn its true distribution, and dynamic target recalibration corrects for the fact that labels keep arriving after training.
BalDRO: A Distributionally Robust Optimization based Framework for Large Language Model UnlearningWWW
uses Remove targeted knowledge from language models by heavily weighting the hardest samples to forget, finding parameter changes that erase them without breaking everything else.
why it works Hard-to-forget samples need more emphasis or they slip through; focusing on the worst-case samples forces the model to handle them, and optimizing against that worst case prevents the easy samples from being over-erased.
From Insight to Intervention: Interpretable Neuron Steering for Controlling Popularity Bias in Recommender SystemsWWW
uses Fix popularity bias in recommendations by identifying which internal neurons fire for popular items, then damping those specific neurons.
why it works Each neuron encodes one type of signal; if you can see which ones encode popularity and turn them down, recommendations shift toward fairness without having to redesign the whole system.
DIARY: Differentially Private Recovery with Adaptive Privacy Budgets in Federated UnlearningWWW
uses Adaptively split the privacy budget across training and recovery phases, then detect anomalies to recover the model while minimizing both privacy leakage and overhead.
why it works It works because different phases need different privacy protection levels; anomaly detection identifies when attacks occur so recovery can happen selectively, letting you use your privacy budget where it matters most.
Post-Training Fairness Control: A Single-Train Framework for Dynamic Fairness in RecommendationWWW
uses Train once on a data representation, then insert different fairness small add-on modules at test time to tune fairness level without retraining.
why it works It works because fairness is a tuning knob, not a fixed property. By learning a shared representation once and plugging in different fairness tweaks later, you avoid the cost of retraining while guaranteeing that fairness improves smoothly as you adjust the dial—each step is strictly more fair than the last.
RoFiRe: Robust Website Fingerprinting on Real-World Tor Traffic via Improved Augmentation and NormalizationWWW
uses Learns to recognize website traffic patterns in encrypted data by training on irregular bursts with smart data augmentation.
why it works Works because real patterns repeat even when data is noisy; augmentation makes the learner robust to variations it never exactly saw.
BLEND: Balanced and Leaf-Enhanced Dual Fine-Tuning for Taxonomy CompletionWWW
uses Learns where to place new concepts in a hierarchy by training separately on leaf and non-leaf relations, then combining them.
why it works Works because leaf and non-leaf edges have different patterns; training separately captures each, then contrasting paths unifies them.
Efficient Content-based Recommendation Model Training via Noise-aware Coreset SelectionWWW
uses Selects a tiny subset of the data for training by optimizing which samples matter most, while removing noisy or unreliable interactions.
why it works Most data points contribute equally to improving the model; identifying and keeping only the high-value samples lets you train with far less data. Removing noise ensures those kept samples actually improve rather than mislead.
Self-Speculative Decoding for On-device MoE AccelerationWWW
uses Routes simple queries to lightweight draft experts and complex ones to full verification, adaptively choosing when to compute deeply.
why it works It works because query difficulty varies hugely. Most queries are simple facts requiring no reasoning, so skipping expensive reasoning for easy cases saves time without sacrificing answers.
Rethinking Soft Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Query-Conditioned Selector PerspectiveWWW
uses Trains a selector to extract only the parts of a document most relevant to the user's query, rather than compressing the entire document equally, and learns weights through training on question-answer pairs.
why it works Full compression forces the system to preserve all information, including irrelevant details, diluting signal. Selective extraction weights query-relevant content high, so the compressed output concentrates only what the language model needs to answer correctly.
TOOL-CURE: Tool Selection via Curriculum-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning with Sample Screening for LLMsWSDM
uses Train a language model to choose the right tool by starting with easy tool-choices first, then harder ones, while down-weighting bad training examples.
why it works It works because easier tasks build foundational understanding that helps with harder tasks, and discarding noisy training examples prevents learning false patterns that lead to wrong choices.
TemporalExpertNet: Cross-Temporal Knowledge Reuse for Promotion-Aware CVR PredictionWSDM
uses Predict which users will buy during sales by learning stable patterns from past data, then using different expert models to adapt for each sale season.
why it works It works because user behavior has both unchanging patterns and sale-specific shifts; separating stable from temporary patterns lets you reuse past knowledge while adapting to new seasons.
Bootstrapping in the Loop: Multi-hop Question Answering via Alternating Decomposition and RetrievalWSDM
uses Improve question-answering by cycling between breaking complex questions into simpler steps and fetching evidence, where each cycle uses what was learned before to ask better questions.
why it works It works because the two halves feed each other: better evidence helps you ask better subquestions, and better subquestions pull in better evidence, so alternating creates a spiral that reaches deeper understanding than either alone.
Adaptive and Reinforcement-Guided Contrastive Hypergraph DistillationWSDM
uses Teach a small model to mimic a larger graph model's behavior by using contrast—pushing it to match the teacher's answer on correct cases and learn its own good representations on the side.
why it works It works because small models learn faster from examples than from theory, so showing them high-performing teacher outputs as targets plus letting them build confidence through internal contrast prevents copying errors.
Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Accurate Item/Feature Selection in Conversational Recommender SystemsWSDM
uses Select which items to recommend and then select their key features through step-by-step reasoning to filter out irrelevant knowledge.
why it works Information retrieval returns both relevant and irrelevant passages. By forcing the system to explicitly choose which item matters first, then which features of that item matter, you create checkpoints that filter noise at each stage rather than trying to separate them all at once.
Automated C Vulnerability Detection via Structure-Enhanced Graph Transformer and RBMWSDM
uses Capture both code structure and hidden semantic patterns using joint feature extraction, then focus on vulnerability paths during detection.
why it works Real vulnerabilities hide in combinations of structure and meaning that simple patterns miss. By mining hidden patterns jointly with visible structure, you find weaknesses that surface-level syntax won't catch. Tracking paths during detection lets the model explain why each vulnerability matters.
SoftHist: Teaching Graph Injection Attackers to Camouflage with MemoryWSDM
uses Use reinforcement learning to select attack strategies that maximize deception while avoiding detection, guided by a learned policy that reuses past decisions to adapt to defenses.
why it works It works because adversarial attack success requires balancing two goals: fooling the system and staying hidden. Reinforcement learning finds the path downhill toward both goals simultaneously. Reusing past attack memories teaches the learner which moves work against specific defenses.
A New Attack Surface: XAI-guided Adversarial Comment Generation with LLMs to Attack Fake News DetectorsWSDM
uses Identify which words drive fake-news detection decisions, then prompt a language model to write human-like comments using those influential words, crafted to flip the classifier's judgment.
why it works It works because classifiers have weak spots: certain features carry outsized influence on the decision. By spotlighting those features and generating text around them, the attack exploits the model's own reasoning against it. Feature importance shows which words the detector trusts most, making those the target.
Mitigating the Threshold Priming Effect in Large Language Model–Based Relevance Judgments via Personality SimulationWSDM
uses Assign personality traits to language models and measure how different personalities change their susceptibility to biased labeling, then use high-performing personalities to reduce bias in relevance judgments.
why it works It works because bias is a learned pattern: models absorb it from training data. Personality prompting changes which learned patterns activate, suppressing biases in some personality profiles. High-Openness personalities, for instance, activate reasoning patterns that question first impressions rather than anchoring to them.
TRACE: A Scalable and Extensible Framework for Auditing YouTube's Recommendation AlgorithmWSDM
uses Simulate diverse user personas over time, trace their YouTube recommendations, log the results in a database, then analyze which features and behaviors drive algorithmic personalization and filter bubbles.
why it works It works because personalization leaves traces: each user action feeds back into the algorithm. By simulating many personas, you observe the full feedback loop. Logging and tracing reveal which user signals the system weighs most and how recommendations drift as personas interact, making the invisible algorithm visible.
ARROW: Adaptive Reasoning for LLM-based Recommendation with ExplainabilityWSDM
uses Prompt a language model to explain its recommendation reasoning step-by-step, then learn a modifier that weighs how much to trust each reasoning step based on uncertainty, balancing explanation with prediction accuracy.
why it works It works because language models contain rich reasoning but sometimes generate plausible-sounding nonsense. Uncertainty quantification identifies shaky reasoning steps. By weighting down uncertain explanations while keeping good ones, the system extracts the true reasoning the model learned, connecting predictions to trustworthy logic.
ACE: Semantically-Grounded Graph Alignment via Affective Contrastive LearningSIGIR
uses Learn item similarities by contrasting user preferences, weighting the contrast loss to align numeric fingerprints with emotional meaning (valence and arousal) extracted from language models.
why it works It works because items users treat similarly should sit close in learned space. By weighting similarity comparisons according to the emotional tone users assign to items, you ensure the learned closeness reflects what matters to the user, not just structure.
Depression Detection from Social Media: A Mutual Guidance Multi-modal Network with Complementary Graph LearningSIGIR
uses Predict depression risk by building a graph of visual and audio similarities, then weighting each modality's contribution adaptively based on what the graph reveals about complementary information.
why it works It works because mental distress shows across multiple modalities in overlapping but distinct ways: voice tone and facial expression both signal depression, yet neither alone is complete. Building a shared graph forces the model to find where modalities align versus diverge, and weighting by that structure preserves both unique and overlapping signals.
NeuCon-ICE: Neuron-Level Controllable In-Context Editing for Multimodal Large Language ModelsSIGIR
uses Correct outdated knowledge in large multimodal models by identifying the specific neurons responding to a fact, then injecting context-aware corrections directly into those neurons.
why it works It works because knowledge localizes: specific neurons handle specific facts. By pinpointing and updating only those neurons rather than retraining everything, the model applies precise corrections without disrupting unrelated knowledge. Neuron-level surgery is surgical—it avoids collateral damage to other capabilities.
Mitigating Evidence Suppression: Bi-level Active Evidence Injection for Educational Video UnderstandingSIGIR
uses Inject evidence words into the model during decoding with learned weights, prioritizing words that are critical to the answer and suppressing ones that distract.
why it works It works because evidence matters differently depending on where in the reasoning you are. By learning to weight each evidence words's contribution based on the task and where you are in decoding, you boost the most critical clues at each step while cutting noise. Different tasks need different evidence emphasized.
A Parametric Memory Head for Continual Generative RetrievalSIGIR
uses Add a memory module that stores corrections for new documents alongside an existing ranking model, freezing the model while only updating memory weights.
why it works It works because memory is modular—new facts can be stored in a table without overwriting old patterns. By separating knowledge storage from core learning, you retain old knowledge while efficiently absorbing new documents.
Multi-modal Relational Item Representation Learning for Inferring Substitutable and Complementary ItemsSIGIR
uses Combines product descriptions and user behavior to learn which items are interchangeable and which complement each other.
why it works It works because items recommended together or by the same people tend to be substitutes or complements; weighting clean signals more than noisy ones extracts that true relationship.
When and How to Ask: Dynamic Preference Elicitation Strategies for Conversational RecommendationSIGIR
uses The system learns to pick the best question strategy for each conversation stage—asking about product features early and specific items later—by scoring which strategy fits the current dialogue state.
why it works It works because users have different information needs at different conversation points. By learning when each strategy works best and weighting them accordingly, the system adapts its questions to match what will actually help narrow down preferences most effectively at each moment.
Discrete Preference Learning for Personalized Multimodal GenerationSIGIR
uses Learn which user preferences matter most for each content type separately, then convert those learned weights into discrete words that control text and image generation.
why it works It works because different content types (text vs. image) matter differently to users. Learning separate preference models lets you capture modal-specific signals, and quantizing into words makes preferences actionable for generators that consume discrete input.
Understanding Wacky Weights: A Dissection of SPLADE's Learned Term ImportanceSIGIR
uses Learn which terms are useful for retrieval by assigning learned weights to vocabulary words, investigating why some weights point to unrelated words and how sparsity keeping it simple affects this.
why it works Learned term weighting works because the model can learn the true predictive power of each term from training data. But larger vocabularies and loose keeping it simple let the model assign weight to terms that happen to correlate with queries in the training set without being semantically meaningful.
Comparing Token Pruning Approaches for Multi-Vector RetrievalSIGIR
uses Reduce computational cost in multi-lists of numbers retrieval by pruning lists of numbers based on learned importance weights or statistical rarity, testing effectiveness-efficiency trade-offs.
why it works It works because most lists of numbers contribute little to the final score—pruning removes redundant ones. Weighted pruning learns which words actually aid discrimination, while simple pruning based on statistics still removes enough noise to keep top results intact when the model is trained with pruning in mind.
From Continuous Pretraining to Domain-Adaptive Reranking via Task Vector AdaptationSIGIR
uses Learn per-parameter weights to combine domain-specific knowledge (from pretraining) with reranking objectives, keeping all weights fixed.
why it works It works because different parts of the model contribute differently to domain adaptation. By learning which parts of the pretrained knowledge matter most for each domain and weighting them individually, the model transfers domain expertise smoothly without catastrophic forgetting.
Revisiting the Role of Learned Attention Weighting in SASRecSIGIR
uses Replace learned importance weights with uniform weights in a recommendation model and measure whether the predictions change, revealing if the model truly uses the weights.
why it works If uniform weights produce similar results to learned weights, the model is not exploiting importance ranking; if results differ, it shows learned weighting is functionally important.
Reward Shaping for Robust Refusal in Small Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question AnsweringSIGIR
uses Teach models to reason step by step through documents and refuse to answer when evidence is absent, using rewards that mark correct refusals highly.
why it works Models naturally output answers because they're trained to be helpful. By rewarding refusals as much as correct answers, you reweight what the model learns is valuable—refusal becomes the right move when documents don't support the claim, because that's now the praised outcome.
Temporal User-Agnostic Ranking: Detecting Preference Evolution while Preserving Ethical PrinciplesSIGIR
uses Weight recent ratings more heavily and detect when rating patterns genuinely change versus when they're just noise, without storing user profiles.
why it works Old ratings should matter less because preferences drift. By applying exponential decay, recent signals get more say. Change detection distinguishes real shifts from random variation—making adaptation possible without ever storing who rated what, so no privacy or bias issues arise.
Structural and Disentangled Adaptation of Large Vision Language Models for Multimodal RecommendationSIGIR
uses Align images and text to preserve internal structure, then learn separate learning paths for each modality to prevent one mode from hijacking the slope.
why it works A large pretrained model knows both images and text, but domain-specific items look different from web images it learned on. By using image structure as a guide for text alignment, you remind the model what the domain looks like. Separate learning paths prevent the slope from one mode drowning out the other, so each signals gets heard.
Teaching Small Models When Not to Call Functions: Structured Reasoning for Tool Refusal in Low-Resource LanguagesSIGIR
uses Train small models to output step-by-step reasoning (task understanding, tool assessment, risk evaluation) before deciding whether to call a tool, weighting each reasoning stage.
why it works Breaking a decision into explicit stages makes the model learn the true factors that matter for refusing tools: understanding the task, assessing if any tool fits, and catching when calling would hallucinate. The stages internalize the real decision logic.
Selective Distillation for Continual Named Entity Recognition with Memory ReplaySIGIR
uses Identify which neurons matter for old tasks and preserve them with distillation loss, while replaying memories of past entities to balance learning new ones without forgetting.
why it works Important neurons encode core patterns that transfer across tasks. By constraining them to stay stable during new learning, you prevent catastrophic forgetting. Memory replay adds back old examples so slope don't fully erase them.
Differentiable Dual Anchor Negative Sampling for Graph-based RecommendationSIGIR
uses Learning to pick hard negative examples during training by scoring items from two angles (user and item perspectives) while keeping slope flowing through the selection process.
why it works The method works because using multiple viewpoints catches negatives that any single perspective would miss, and keeping slope flowing means the model can adjust its negative choices as it improves, creating a feedback loop that tightens the training signal.
Efficient Memory Alignment for Long-term Conversational Information SeekingSIGIR
uses For a chatbot with a long memory, the system decides which memory facts to write, update, or keep by retrieving similar past entries and scoring them based on how important they are to the current conversation.
why it works It works because facts that keep appearing across conversations reveal what is truly important to the person; by checking what already exists before adding new facts, redundancy goes down, and by weighing importance, the memory stays compact for fast retrieval.
SCORE-RAG: Self-Correcting Exploration-Exploitation Retrieval for Multi-hop Question AnsweringSIGIR
uses For questions with multiple hops, first explore broadly to understand what the question is really asking and find key entities, then focus retrieval on gathering evidence that chains together to answer it.
why it works It works because complex questions are ambiguous: you can interpret them multiple ways, and each interpretation retrieves different things; exploring first resolves the ambiguity by checking what entities and concepts the question connects to, then focused retrieval avoids wasting effort on wrong paths.
When &#38; How to Write for Personalized Demand-aware Query Rewriting in Video SearchSIGIR
uses The system learns when personalization helps and how to rewrite queries in a way that matches the retrieval system, trained on examples mined from real user logs.
why it works Most rewrites hurt; personalizing too much adds noise. By mining examples where users explicitly reformulated queries themselves, the model learns the signal from the noise. Training jointly with both supervised and reinforcement learning ensures outputs align with what the retrieval system actually needs.
Gated Bidirectional Linear Attention for Generative RetrievalSIGIR
uses Processes long user histories using bidirectional linear-time focus that forgets old events gradually and gates output, avoiding quadratic slowdown.
why it works It works because share-of-total weighting focus has to process every past event equally, so long histories explode in cost. Linear focus with forgetting gates keeps the cost flat while mimicking bidirectional bidirectional focus's quality. Conv1D mixes local context, RMSNorm stabilizes slope.
Policy-Guided RAG: Enforcing Verbatim and Controlled SynthesisSIGIR
uses Routes retrieved sensitive content through one of three handling modes: quote verbatim, blend while minimizing exposure, or synthesize without using sensitive parts.
why it works It works because different use cases need different trade-offs between utility and compliance. Metadata tags let the system make mode decisions before generating. Auditing the final output catches slips. This separates routing (which requires context) from enforcement (which can be checked mechanically).
Query-Attention Dual-Stream Framework with Cross-Category Transfer for Efficient Fine-Grained Interest Pre-RankingSIGIR
uses Attend to query-relevant user behaviors, then learn from dense domains and transfer the patterns to sparse domains using contrastive comparison.
why it works It works because focus focuses resources on signals that matter most for the query, reducing wasted computation. Contrastive transfer works because dense domains already have strong patterns that, when properly aligned, teach the model to recognize similar patterns in sparse data.
WeSEAL: Well-calibrated Search for Eliminating Attention-sink LeakageSIGIR
uses Train the model to suppress focus to early documents regardless of content and redirect focus to semantic relevance signals instead.
why it works It works because models learn what they are trained to do. If you explicitly train the model to align focus with semantic relevance rather than position, the model internalizes this behavior. The bias gets baked into parameters, not requiring expensive correction at test time.
AIPO: Adaptive Anchored Intent-aware Policy Optimization for Generative RecommendationSIGIR
uses A learned policy selects which user behaviors to amplify and which feedback signals to trust, rejecting noisy click signals to reduce reward hacking and improve stability.
why it works Noisy feedback leads to unstable slope and the model exploits the noise rather than learning real patterns. By learning to upweight high-confidence signals and downweight low-signal data, you reduce spread of error in the slope updates, stabilizing learning toward the true reward.
IR Lens: A Tool for Interpreting Cross-Encoder ModelsSIGIR
uses Neural ranking models are analyzed by computing which neurons contribute most to each ranking decision through integrated slope analysis and targeted ablations.
why it works Neural models compute via thousands of intermediate states; you cannot see ranking logic by reading weights. Integrated slope trace how much each neuron causally impacts the output by computing the sum of slope along a path from zero to the actual input. This reveals cause-and-effect in the model, enabling diagnosis and improvement.
Topology-Conditioned Weak Supervision for Scientific RetrievalSIGIR
uses Weight heuristic signals for relevance based on their reliability as a function of where documents sit in the citation network.
why it works It works because citation topology reveals trustworthiness: papers heavily cited by peers in a topic are more likely to be truly relevant. Heuristic signals' reliability varies by position (central papers have stronger signals), so using network position to adjust signal weights improves weak supervision quality.
53 papers

Finding the least-wrong settings

Almost every learned system is tuned the same way: define a single number for how wrong it currently is, then adjust its internal settings to make that number as small as possible.

Why it works — the principle

It works because the slope of how-wrong tells you exactly which small adjustment reduces the error, so nudging that way over and over can only improve, and it settles where no small change helps. When the error surface is bowl-shaped that settling point is the best possible; even when it is rugged, this reliably reaches a good one.

Meta-Learning Driven Few-Shot Knowledge Transfer with Dual-Stage Adaptive Data Replay for Cross-Domain RecommendationWWW
uses Learn flexible alignment rules between recommendation domains using few examples, then replay refined data to reduce transfer mistakes.
why it works By adjusting how knowledge transfers based on overlapping examples, the model avoids rigid alignment rules that fail in new scenarios and catches negative transfer before it harms recommendations.
Better Negatives, Better Predictions: Negative Sample Selection Strategies for Enhancing Biomedical KG Edge ClassificationWWW
